No. 3 thereof omitted by virtue of amendment vide Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Chhattisgarh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 2.2 to 2.4 and 7 to 10] [In favour of revenue]  Railway - Interpretation of - Term 'pertaining to Railways' occurring in Entry 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 covers both Government Railway as well as non-Government Railway and it should be used for public carriage of passengers or goods as stipulated under section 2(31) of Railways Act, 1989 - Railway track meant exclusively for private use of project owners for transport of goods from/upto their plant though constructed by using Rails as per specifications under Act ibid, cannot qualify as 'Railway' and not eligible to exemption thereunder as it is not used for public carriage of passenger or goods [Section 11 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Chhattisgarh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 9.9] [In favour of revenue]   Circulars And Notifications : Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; Notification No. 20/2017, dated 22-7-2017; Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018; Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021 and Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022

Works Contract - Railway project - Appellant was awarded contract for construction of pavement, track work, warehouses, admin building, EM works and other miscellaneous works relating to high speed rail project - AAR has found that works are in nature of new works executed and also gets covered under definition of 'original works' as defined in clause (zs) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Advance ruling was passed holding that impugned works contract does not pertain to railways; hence, not covered under Entry No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and thus, not exigible to reduced GST at rate of 12 per cent instead of 18 per cent - HELD : To build and operate high speed Rail corridor, an SPV has been formed under Ministry of Railways, Government of India; said government body is engaged primarily in work related to railways only - Works contract has been awarded by SPV to main contractor which too is a public sector undertaking - Said Main contractor has sub-contracted it to appellant - As per letter of acceptance issued by SPV to main contractor, work pertains to shifting of existing railway infrastructure and other utilities in connection with construction of High Speed Rail Project - As per tender and other documents, work allotted to appellant is with regard to railways - Various items of work as per documents pertain to railways only - Conditions stipulated in Entry 3(v)(a) of impugned notification are fulfilled - Impugned activity is works contract involving original work pertaining to railways - Therefore, reduced GST of 12 per cent would be applicable [Paras 13, 16 to 20] [In favour of applicant]GST : Sub-contractor undertaking works contract relating to construction of pavement, track work, etc., pertaining to High Speed Rail Project is entitled to concessional GST rate of 12 per cent

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Supply and installation - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFFCCIL) has awarded a contract to one 'A' (main contractor) for performance of works relating to design, construction, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of electrification, signaling, telecommunication and associated works of double track railways lines under construction for Bhaupur-Khurja section - 'A' (main contractor) has subcontracted performance of certain works and services of main contract to applicant - Whether contract work of applicant to main contractor is covered under Entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to tax at 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST or 12 per cent IGST) with effect from 22-8-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 4.10 and 5][In favour of assessee]GST: Where Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited has awarded a contract to one 'A' (main contractor) for performance of works relating to railways and 'A' has sub-contracted performance of certain works and services of main contract to applicant, contract work of applicant to main contractor is covered under Entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant has constructed residential complexes for Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) - Whether since control over BDA rests with Govt. of Karnataka, BDA is a Government entity - Held, yes - Whether activity undertaken by applicant involves supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property and, hence, is a 'works contract' within meaning of section 2(119) - Held, yes - Whether transaction of applicant would be a supply of works contract services covered under clause (a) of Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, taxable at rate of 12 per cent GST - Held, yes [Paras 10.8, 10.9.2  11]GST : Where applicant has constructed residential complexes for Bangalore Development Authority (BDA), activity undertaken by applicant is supply of works contract service to a Govt. entity covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, taxable at rate of 12 per cent GST

Work Contract Services - Composite supply pertaining to railways - Construction service - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Period 2018-19 to 2022-23 - Assessee was a joint venture formed for executing various railway projects in India - Assessee was assigned works contract by RVNL for ‘Doubling of track, construction of roadbed, minor bridges, platforms, buildings, water and effluent treatment facilities, wagon/coach maintenance infrastructure, supply of ballast, installation of tracks and other electrical, signalling, and telecommunication infrastructure’ - During period April, 2018 to March, 2019, assessee paid GST at rate of 12 per cent on above contract - Assessee had discharged taxes at rate of 12 per cent on premise that said contract constitutes works contract services of original works pertaining to Railways covered under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) - Further, assessee was served with an intimation in Form GST DRC-01A - Said notice proceeds on premise that said contract between assessee and RVNL was liable to tax at 18 per cent, instead, assessee had erroneously discharged taxes at a lower/concessional rate of 12 per cent on works contract executed by assessee - Thereafter demand order was also confirmed by revenue for differential tax of 6 per cent - HELD : Expression ‘pertaining to’ employed in said notification with reference to railways is one of very wide import - Use of expression ‘pertaining to’ would show that legislation intended to give an expansive meaning to expression ‘Railway’ - Phrase ‘pertaining to’ has been interpreted in previous Supreme Court rulings as broad and inclusive, covering activities closely related to primary subject - In instant case assessee's contract clearly relates to railway development and expression ‘pertaining to’ ensures that infrastructure projects were aiding railway operations; even if carried out by a subsidiary like RVNL, same would still constitute original work pertaining to railway for purpose of subject notification and, thus, covered under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of said notification - Thus, activity of assessee would be covered under concessional rate and there was no reason to exclude assessee’s works contract from ambit of 12 per cent rate [Section 9, read with section 73, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 16.1 16.2, 17.2 and 18.4] [In favour of assessee]

Railway infrastructure construction - Construction services - Composite supply of works contract - Words contract - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Contract for supply of goods and services was awarded to assessee by RITES Ltd., a Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) on behalf of South Eastern Coalfield Limited (SECL) for construction of railway infrastructure facilities for proposed feeder line of East West Rail Corridor within leasehold boundary of project for coal evacuation through Rail - Aforesaid supply involves supply of goods and services which are supplied in conjunction with each other in ordinary course of business; same is to be considered as composite supply under section 2(30) - Such supply being original work in terms of Para 2(zs) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 pertaining to Railway network owned by a SECL, a PSU is to be considered as original work pertaining to Railways under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and is specifically covered under Heading No. 9954 21 - However, since term Works Contract defined under section 2(119) is restricted to contract for building construction, fabrication etc. of any immovable property only and Letter of acceptance issued by RITES to applicant-assessee only outlines description of their activities which appears to be Project Management Consultancy services, it is not possible to conclusively hold that their activities are covered under Works Contract under said section 2(119) - Hence, works proposed to be performed by them under LOA would attract 12 per cent GST under SL. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended vide Notification No. 1/2018-C.T. (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 subject to condition that same satisfies definition of Works Contract under section 2(119) otherwise it would be taxable at rate of 18 per cent GST under Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Chhattisgarh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 1, 2.2 to 2.4, 7 to 7.8, 7.10 and 8] [Partly in favour of assessee]GST : Supply of goods and services for construction of railway infrastructure facilities for feeder line of Rail Corridor owned by South Eastern Coalfield Limited for evacuation of coal, under contract awarded by RITES, a PSU, is specifically covered under SAC 9954 21 and same is considered to be an original work pertaining to Railways and a composite supply in terms of section 2(30); therefore, such supply would attract 12 per cent GST subject to condition that it satisfies definition of works contract under section 2(119), otherwise it would be taxable at rate of 18 per cent GST   GST : Term 'pertaining to Railways' occurring in Entry 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017as amended includes both Government Railways as well as non-Government Railways

No. 126 of Schedule I to Notification No. 01/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

Construction of railway siding - Construction service - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Public sector undertaking, Rites Limited has, for and on behalf of Eastern Coalfields Limited, awarded applicant different works in connection with construction of new railway siding - Works undertaken by applicant is in relation to immovable property and involve transfer of property in goods thereby qualify to be 'works contract' - Construction work in connection of new railway sidings undertaken by applicant is to be considered as original works as defined in clause 2(zs) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Ministry of Railways, Government of India in its Freight Marketing Circular No. 11 of 2016 issued on 22-8-2016 has also recognized 'private siding' for railway freight services - Therefore, construction of private sidings pertains to railways and is taxable at rate of 12 per cent under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 till its omission

Railway infrastructure construction - General Construction services of highways, streets, roads, railways, etc - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Advance ruling is sought on whether civil works undertaken for Indian government enterprise for railways in connection with construction of rail infrastructure for providing railway siding for dispatch of washed and raw coal is eligible for concessional rate of GST at 12 per cent - HELD: GST is applicable at 12 per cent only when service provided relates to construction and in nature of composite supply of works contract and should qualify as original works pertaining to railways - Work undertaken is covered under "General construction services of highways, streets, roads, railways, airfield runways, bridges and tunnels" classifiable under Heading 9954 - Work undertaken amounts to composite supply or cannot be conclusively answered in absence of sufficient evidence - Although it is apparent from work undertaken that it is supply in relation to immovable property, there must also be transfer of property in goods in execution of contract - Work undertaken for RITES qualifies as original works pertaining to railways which will be liable to GST at 12 per cent if same qualifies as composite supply of works contract [Chhattisgarh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 8] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where works were undertaken for Indian government enterprise for railways namely, RITES qualifies as original work pertaining to railways, GST at 12 per cent will be available if said work qualifies as composite supply of works contract

Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Installation, commissioning and fitting out of a civil structure - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, Department of Space, Government of India entered into a contract with Tata Projects Ltd., Mumbai [applicant] for design, realization, integration and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel at Thiruvananthapuram - Work involves aerodynamic structural and control design analysis, detailed design, detailed engineering, fabrication, procurement, inspection, third party inspection, loading and unloading of material, transportation to site, civil and electrical works, integration of systems, training, documentation, acceptance, testing and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel - Whether supply under contract can be considered as supply of equipment eligible for concessional rate of GST as per Sl. No. 243B of Schedule I of Notification No. 1/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, no - Whether work of design, realization, integration and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel as a turnkey project will fall under definition of works contract - Held, yes - Whether service provided by applicant to Central Government by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession will attract 12 per cent GST as per Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 6] [Partly in favour of assessee]GST : Where Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre entered into a contract with Tata Projects Ltd., Mumbai [applicant] for design, realization, integration and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel, supply under contract cannot be considered as supply of equipment and work as a turnkey project will fall under definition of works contract and service provided by applicant will attract 12 per cent GST

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Civil Construction and works contract services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services)/Section 2(119) of the Central Goods And Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant is engaged in business of Civil Construction and Works Contract Services - It has entered into agreement to undertake subcontract work of civil construction of residential complexes/row of residential houses which in turn has been allotted to GIPL (main contractor) through tender by Bengaluru Development Authority - Whether since projects of applicant are involving supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property it is a 'work contract' within meaning of section 2(119) - Held, yes - Whether works contract is for construction of a civil structure and since it is a residential real estate project, works is predominantly for use other than commerce, industry or any other business or profession and it is covered under clause (a) of entry 3(vi) of Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes - Whether further, since main contractor is providing services specified in item 3(vi) of Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, subcontract work of works contract provided by applicant as a subcontractor to main contractor is covered under item (ix) of entry 3 of Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification No. 1/2018 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, taxable at 6 per cent CGST with effect from 25-1-2018 - Whether however, for period from 1-7-2017 to 24-1-2018, same is taxable at 9 per cent CGST - Held, yes [Paras 11 and 12]GST: Projects of applicant involving work orders from Principal contractor for civil construction of residential complexes consisting of supply of both goods and services in relation to an immovable property is a 'works contract' within meaning of section 2(119)   GST: Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Entity within meaning of Notification No.11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Composite supply of works contract services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant has been awarded contracts by 3 Electric Distribution companies- HESCOM, MESCOM and BESCOM, comprising of work in nature of strengthening of distribution networks on Turnkey Basis, providing infrastructure to regularized IP sets by extending electric lines, erection of distribution transformers, and strengthening works - Contracts executed by applicant are works contract, because (i) they are in relation to completion, erection, installation, and commissioning of an immovable property as all projects are turnkey projects and property in goods cannot be removed without dismantling same, and (ii) there is transfer of property involved in execution of contract - Further, distribution companies are involved in supply of goods and hence are involved in business of supplying goods and also receive consideration for supply of electricity - Predominant activity of electricity distribution companies is to supply electricity and works executed by applicant are used for this predominant activity only and hence are original works meant predominantly for use for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession - Whether therefore, it was to be held that services provided by applicant to Energy Supply Companies (wholly owned Government of Karnataka Undertakings) by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion etc. are not covered under entry 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 12/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, or under entry 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended from time to time and consequently are not eligible to be taxed at a lower rate of 12 per cent GST and hence are liable to be taxed at 18 per cent GST - Held, yes [Paras 11 and 12]GST: Services by way of construction erection, commissioning, installation, completion etc. provided by applicant to Energy Supply Companies(wholly owned Government of Karnataka Undertaking) are liable to be taxed at 18 per cent GST

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 [Construction Services] - Applicant a Private Limited Company entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences(NCBS) for construction of Hostel building at NCBS Campus in Bangalore - It sought advance ruling on whether it should charge GST at rate of 12 per cent for service provided to NCBS as per Notification No 24/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 21-9-2017- It is found that NCBS, which is a separate centre of Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), receives grant from Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India and that NCBS is neither set-up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature nor was established by any Government, but is an autonomous body under aegis of TIFR - Moreover, council administering this institute has only 4 members appointed by Government and therefore Government does not have more than 90 per cent control over it - Thus, NCBS is not covered under definition of a 'Government Entity' as per clause (x) of para 4 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Furthermore, Institute is not established to carry out a function entrusted by Government, thus, it is not covered by clause (vi) of serial no. 3 of Notification - Whether therefore, service supplied by applicant to NCBS is not taxable at concessional rate of 12 per cent and is taxable at 18 per cent under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 5 and 6]GST: Works contract service provided by applicant to National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) for construction of hostel building on campus is taxable at 18 per cent GST under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant is engaged in business of execution of works contracts relating to electrical works and electrical infrastructure - Applicant has been allocated electrical sub-contractor works by first sub-contractor 'S' which in turn is sub-contracted by main contractor 'O' who have been awarded contract by 'K' for civil, electrical and mechanical works - 'K' is a company which is wholly owned by Government of Karnataka - Whether since there is no privity of contract between applicant and main contractor i.e., 'O' and contract is between applicant and 'S' 'which is not covered under Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority or a Governmental Authority or Government Entity, supply made by applicant is not covered under Entry No. 3 (iii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes - Whether activity of applicant is also not covered under Entry Nos. 3(vi) and 3(ix) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes - Whether thus, composite supply undertaken by applicant is not covered under Entry No. 3(iii) or 3(vi) or 3(ix) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and, hence, applicant is not eligible to charge GST at a concessional rate of 12 per cent - Held, yes - Whether applicant has to discharge tax at rate of 18 per cent under provision of GST Act - Held, yes [Paras 9.4, 10.2, 10.3 and 12]GST : Where applicant has been allocated electrical sub-contractor works by first sub-contractor 'S' which in turn is sub-contracted by main contractor 'O' who have been awarded contract by 'K' for civil, electrical and mechanical works, composite supply undertaken by applicant is not covered under Entry No. 3(iii) or 3(vi) or 3(ix) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and, hence, applicant is not eligible to charge GST at concessional rate of 12 per cent and is liable to GST at rate of 18 per cent

Construction of Roads and Bridges - Construction Services - Heading 9954 - Classification - Applicant is a contractor engaged in construction of roads and bridges - Applicant seeks advance ruling on what is GST rate on works contract services provided by a Government Contractor to KSTP, construction of Roads and bridges for public use?- Held : In instant case, recipient of applicant i.e., Kerala State Transport Project (KSTP) is a wing constituted under Kerala Public Works Department was to execute externally aided projects and specialized projects - Main aim of this wing is upgradation of State highway roads - Strategic option study made for upgradation of State highways and major district roads led to formation of KSTP under Kerala Public Works Department - Government had accepted study report and accorded administrative sanction for upgradation of 1719.46 kilometers of roads vide GO (MS). 142/97/PWD dated 22-12-1997 of Public Works (D) Department, Government of Kerala through KSTP with aid of World Bank - Hence, works contract services provided by applicant to KSTP by way of construction of roads and bridges is for use of general public - As such, rate of tax for works contract services provided by applicant to KSTP by way of construction of roads and bridges for public use will be taxable at 12 per cent (CGST at rate 6 per cent and SGST at rate 6 per cent) - Further, as per Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 amended by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022, it is evident that till 17-7-2022, rate of tax for works contract services by way of construction of roads and bridges for public use was 12 per cent (CGST at rate 6 per cent and SGST at rate 6 per cent), if, time of supply as determined in accordance with section 14 falls any date prior to 18-7-2022, otherwise it will be taxable at 18 per cent (CGST at rate 9 per cent and SGST at rate 9 per cent) [Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.6-7.10] [Against assessee]

Main aim of this wing is upgradation of State highway roads - Strategic option study made for upgradation of State highways and major district roads led to formation of KSTP under Kerala Public Works Department - Government had accepted study report and accorded administrative sanction for upgradation of 1719.46 kilometers of roads vide GO (MS). 142/97/PWD dated 22-12-1997 of Public Works (D) Department, Government of Kerala through KSTP with aid of World Bank - Hence, works contract services provided by applicant to KSTP by way of construction of roads and bridges is for use of general public - As such, rate of tax for works contract services provided by applicant to KSTP by way of construction of roads and bridges for public use will be taxable at 12 per cent (CGST at rate 6 per cent and SGST at rate 6 per cent) - Further, as per Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 amended by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022, it is evident that till 17-7-2022, rate of tax for works contract services by way of construction of roads and bridges for public use was 12 per cent (CGST at rate 6 per cent and SGST at rate 6 per cent), if, time of supply as determined in accordance with section 14 falls any date prior to 18-7-2022, otherwise it will be taxable at 18 per cent (CGST at rate 9 per cent and SGST at rate 9 per cent) [Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.6-7.10] [Against assessee]   Circulars and Notifications : Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 amended by Notification No. 03/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022

Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant a proprietary concern was awarded sub-contract works by Principal Contractor to execute sub-station and terminal boy works - Applicant submitted that said works are mainly awarded to principal contractor by State Government entities, hence, supply of services is covered under SI.No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-06-2017 vide HSN code 9954 and attracts 18 per cent GST - However, Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 was amended, as a result of which rate of tax on turnkey projects, which was subcontracted to applicant by principal contractor which in turn was awarded to him by State Government entities attracted GST at rate of 12 per cent - It is found that item no. (ix) of SI.No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 -Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 governs sub-contracts of main contracts where main contract is for provision of composite supply of works contract to Government - For sub-contract to get included in this item, main contract between principal contractor and Government entity should relate to supply of works contract services specified in item no. (iii) and (vi) - However, it is found that contract between main contractor and Government entity is for supply, design, erection, transmission and commissioning of different capacity of transformers and this supply is neither covered under item (iii) nor item (vi), hence, supply of services by applicant is not covered under item no. (ix) -Whether therefore, this supply would get covered only under item (ii) of SI.No. 3 of Notification No.11/2017 -Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 taxable at 18 per cent GST and amendments to Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 would have no effect on taxability of transactions of applicant -Held, yes [Paras 7.9 and 8]GST: Subcontract of design, testing, commissioning and transmission of transformers awarded to principal contractor by State Government entities is a composite supply of works contract and is liable to 18 per cent GST

Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract -  Applicant, a Central Government Department, awarded a works contract to one 'T' for design, fabrication, procurement, instrumentation and control and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel with Ejector System - Work involves fabrication of machineries, transportation of equipments to be attached to system, construction of civil structure where machinery is to be installed - Whether work of design, realisation, integration and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel as a turnkey project will fall under definition of works contract - Held, yes [Para 4] [In favour of assessee] Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction, erection, commissioning, installation of a civil structure - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Applicant, a Central Government Department, awarded a works contract to one 'T' for design, fabrication, procurement, instrumentation and control and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel with Ejector System - Work involves fabrication of machineries, transportation of equipments to be attached to system, construction of civil structure where machinery is to be installed - Whether service provided to applicant will attract 12 per cent GST as per Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 4] [In favour of assessee]  Circulars and Notifications: Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, Notification No. 1/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, Notification No. 7/2018 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 and Notification No. 24/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017  (NR)

Classification of services - West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Erection, commissioning and installation of original work pertaining to railways - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Applicant is engaged in activity of providing technological and system solutions - Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) awarded it contract for extension of its Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) - Applicant makes supply to 'RVNL' by way of erection, commissioning, installation, completion etc. of said SCADA system - Whether, in view of facts, applicant is making a composite supply of works contract taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as being erection, commissioning and installation of original work pertaining to railways, including metro - Held, yes [Para 4.10]GST: Where Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) awarded a contract to applicant for 'extension of its Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) and applicant makes supply to RVNL by way of erection, commissioning, installation, completion etc. of SCADA system, applicant is making a composite supply of works contract taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as being erection, commissioning and installation of original work pertaining to railways, including metro

Classification of services - West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 [Construction Services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works Contract - Appellant, a supplier of works contract service, entered into an agreement with IWAI, a statutory body established under Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985, for construction of multi-modal IWT Terminal at Haldia on EPC (Engineering, Procurement, Construction) basis - Whether since appellant is supplying works contract services to IWAI, a Government entity, for an original work that is meant for infrastructural development of waterways of India and is not meant for commerce or business, amendment to Serial No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, brought about by Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated Notification No. 21-9-2017 and Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017 are applicable to appellant's supply of 'Works Contract Service' towards IWAI for construction of Multi-modal IWT Terminal and, therefore, supply of service by appellant is taxable at rate of 12 per cent - Held, yes [Para 10][In favour of assessee]GST: Where appellant is supplying works contract services to IWAI, a Government entity, for an original work that is meant for infrastructure development of waterways of India and is not meant for commerce or business, amendment to Serial No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is applicable to appellant's supply of works contract service and, therefore, supply of service by appellant is taxable at rate 12 per cent

I. Classification of services - Telangana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract services involving laying of electric power lines - Heading 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant, a Government Entity, supplied works contract services involving laying of electric power lines to Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) - It engaged a private contractor on back to back arrangement for executing works for GHMC - Whether supply of works contract services by applicant to GHMC is covered by Service Code 9954 23 and is taxable at rate of 9 per cent under both CGST Act and SGST Act respectively as per Entry at Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes - Whether service supplied by contractor to applicant is taxable at rate of 9 per cent under both CGST Act and SGST Act respectively as per Entry at Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 7(1) and 7(2)]GST : Where applicant, a Government Entity, supplied works contract services involving laying of electric power lines to Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) and it engaged a private contractor on back to back arrangement for executing works for GHMC, supply of service by applicant to GHMC is covered by Service Code 9954 23 and is taxable at rate of 18 per cent  GST : Where applicant, a Government Entity, made construction of electricity transmission infrastructure to pumping stations under various lift irrigation schemes and State Government sanctions grants to applicant for this purpose and applicant engaged a private turnkey contractor on back to back arrangement for purpose of executing contracts to I  CAD department, applicant is eligible for exemption from tax vide Entry 9(c) of Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017  GST : Where applicant, a Government Entity, is supplying works contract services to South Central Railways under General Construction service for long-distance underground/overland/submarine pipe lines, communication and electric power lines (cables) and it engaged a private turnkey contractor on a back to back arrangement to execute contract for South Central Railways, supply of services by applicant to South Central Railways is taxable at rate of 18 per cent as per Entry at Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Karnataka Residential Educational Institutions Society (KRIES) is formed under societies Registration Act and Government of Karnataka may appoint persons to review progress of society and to hold inquiries into affairs of society and give directions; hence, qualifies to be considered as a Government Entity - Works contract services executed for Construction of Residential school complex are liable to GST at 18 per cent with effect from 1-1-2022 as per Entry No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021 and Notification No. 03/2022 - Central Tax (Rate), dated : 13-7-2022 [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.3 and 14] [In favour of revenue]

facts.text: The applicant was engaged in providing works contract service as sub-contract to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways. The assessee filed instant application to sought clarification for rate of tax to be levied by it to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways. The assessee submitted that it should be charged 12 per cent GST only and not 18 per cent as applicable in other cases.

The applicant is contractor with railways and it has been awarded a contract with KSR Bengaluru City Railway Station and service buildings at Bangalore.

The contract includes new works, repair works, addition and alteration to existing structures.

The applicant states that the Railway is considering all service buildings as business/commerce establishments and rate charged is 18 per cent (even for original works) and works related to all welfare buildings (i.e., only colonies) are charged at 12 per cent.

The applicant is seeking advance ruling as regards applicability of GST rate for works contract services doing original works with Railways.

The applicant has been awarded a contract by one Rites Limited, which is a Public Sector Undertaking. Said contract is awarded for execution of works of laying of track as per layout plan, pavement along the track, construction of Admin building, Warehouse, Electrical works and Fire-fighting works, etc. at Khodiyar Gandhinagar, Gujarat. Further contract is involving both supply of goods and services and is a composite supply in the nature of works contract supply.

The applicant sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

Whether the said work can be covered under clause 3(v)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, i.e., works contract by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to railways so as the entitle it for charging rate of GST at the rate of 12 per cent instead of 18 per cent.

The applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways. It executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract.

It sought advance ruling on the following questions:

1.

What tax rate to be charged by the applicant to main contractor on works contract services pertaining to railways original works contract.

2.

Whether to charge tax rate of 12 per cent GST or 18 per cent GST.

The Authority for Advance Rulings ruled that

-

The tax rate to be charged by the applicant to the main contractor would be at the rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST.

-

The tax rate to be charged would be 12 per cent.

On appeal to Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling by revenue:

The applicant is engaged in execution of works contact awarded by Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Ltd. ('KPTCL'), for construction of power lines, erection of transmission towers and transformers.

The contract with KPTCL is a single contract, but with three connected agreements for supply of materials, erection and civil works, respectively, in response to a single tender notification.

Applicant sought advance ruling on questions as to whether the contract, executed by them for KPTCL, is a divisible contract (Supply of goods and supply of services) or an indivisible contract (works contract) and whether the tax rate of 12 per cent (CGST 6 per cent + SGST 6 per cent) is applicable to the above contract, KPTCL being a statutory body.

The applicant a proprietary concern entered into subcontract agreement with MEIL (Principal Contractor), for design, testing, commissioning of transmission of towers and was awarded subcontract works by the Principal Contractor on 12-10-2018, to execute the substation and terminal bay works.

The above said works were mainly awarded to the Principal Contractor by the state government entities such as Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigam Limited, Karnataka Neeravari Nigam Limited and Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited. The said works have been awarded prior to GST but the same have been amended during the post-GST period.

The applicant has sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

1.

What is rate of tax applicable to the composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of Section 2 of Central Goods and Services Act, 2017 (The Act), undertaken by the supplier (applicant) i.e., whether the GST rate 18 per cent or 12 per cent is to be charged by the supplier?

2.

If the GST rate 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST+ 9 per cent SGST) as prescribed in serial No. 3, against heading No. 9954 (construction services), specified in Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, is the rate applicable to the nature of works contract undertaken by the applicant, kindly clarify the following related aspects also:

The Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, has been amended by:

i.

Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017;

ii.

Notification No: 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017;

iii.

Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018;

Wherein the GST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) has been notified in respect of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2.

If so, whether it would be in order for the applicant (supplier) to charge GST at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST+6 per cent SGST) or is the GST rate 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST+ 9 per cent SGST) applicable to the nature of works contract undertaken by the applicant?

The applicant is engaged in the business of Civil Construction and Works Contract Services. The applicant has applied for the civil construction work tender with Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) with respect to construction of residential complexes/row of residential houses.

The said project is allotted to the applicant and the same has been executed by the Company through appointing various contractors.

The applicant has sought advance ruling in respect of the question as to whether the activity undertaken by the applicant is covered under section 2(119); whether Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Authority as per the provisions of GST Law and the rate of tax applicable to the transaction of the applicant and more so whether the transactions are covered under entry 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 (as amended).

According to applicant, its activity of construction of residential house and residential complex with respect to following BDA projects (to Government Authority) are squarely covered under the definition of Works Contract and their activity will be considered as supply of services.

The applicant submits that as per the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), the activity undertaken by the applicant to BDA i.e., Government Authority is liable for GST at 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST.

The applicant, a Central Government Department, awarded a works contract to Tata Projects Ltd. for design, fabrication, procurement, instrumentation and control and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel with Ejector System. The work involves fabrication of machineries, transportation of equipments to be attached to the system, construction of civil structure where the machinery is to be installed.

It sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

If the above supply is considered as works contract, whether it would be covered under Entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 24/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017 attracting GST at the rate of 12 per cent.

The applicant is engaged in electrification work in the rural and urban areas.

The applicant for the above purpose also receives work contract services from vendors for supply and erection work under various projects.

The applicant wishes to know whether clause (vi)(a) of Sr. No. 3 of table of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is applicable on the works contract services received by it and for determination of liability to pay tax.

The department submitted that the nature of works contract undertaken by the applicant doesn't come under the category for which the notified rate of tax is 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST) but it will attract 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST and 9 per cent SGST).

Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) has awarded the work of execution of civil works of Hydroelectric Project to the appellant. The work involves construction of intake structure, leading channel, tunnel, powerhouse, tail race, civil works of switch yard, access roads and other allied works.

The appellant had filed an application for advance ruling with regard to whether the execution of the civil works of Pazhassi Sagar Small Hydroelectric would fall under Sl. No. 3(iii)(b) or 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 attracting GST at the rate of 12 per cent and whether the rate of SGST is also 6 per cent in terms of Notification SRO 370/2017, dated 30-6-2017 for supplies covered under Work Order 06/CE CCN/2017-18, dated 6-10-2017.

The Advance ruling authority held that where appellant had been awarded work of execution of civil works of Hydroelectric Project in existing dam, it cannot be considered as civil work for canal, dam or other irrigation works eligible for concessional rate of tax but it is works contract services and rate of 6 per cent under Sl. No. 3(iii) or Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is not applicable for said services.

On appeal:

The appellant is a supplier of works contract service and has entered into an agreement with IWAI, a statutory body established under the Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985, for construction of a multi-modal IWT terminal at Haldia, West Bengal on EPC (Engineering, Procurement, Construction) basis.

The appellant sought an Advance Ruling on the question as to applicability of Notification No. 24/2017-CT (Rate), dated 21-9-2017 and 31/2017 Central tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017 and what rate at which GST should be charged on the works contract service supplied for construction of a multi-modal terminal at Haldia, West Bengal.

The West Bengal Authority for Advance Ruling held that amendments to Serial No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 brought about by Notification No. 24/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017 and 31/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017, are not applicable to the applicant's supply of works contract service for construction of the Multi-modal IWT Terminal at Haldia. It will attract GST at 18 per cent rate under Serial No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

The appellant has filed the instant appeal against the Advance Ruling with the prayer to set aside the impugned Advance Ruling passed by the WBAAR on the grounds that IWAI, is a Government Entity and hence the supply of service by the appellant is taxable at the rate of 12 per cent under the GST Act in terms of Serial No. 3(vi) of the Rate Notification as amended.

The applicant-company (MPPGCL) is engaged in carrying out the works contract in relation to construction of road, bridges, buildings, civil structures of Government, semi-Government and private undertakings.

The applicant was awarded a contract for construction of 599 flats by MPPGCL.

During the course of carrying out the construction work, the applicant company raised Running Bills (RA bills) for the portion of work completed at a point of time to MPPGCL by charging CGST and SGST at the rate of 9 per cent each, in view of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017.

MPPGCL is of the opinion that in the work under reference, the applicable rate of GST should be 12 per cent (6+6), as per Notification No.11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, by treating itself as a Government entity and the work allocated to the service provider is the work which is the work supplied to it by the Government.

The applicant seeks advance ruling on issue as to whether MPPGCL is a 'Government Entity' and whether the work contract service of construction of 599 residential quarters allotted to the applicant company, will be charged under the GST rate of 12 per cent (6+6) or 18 per cent (9+9).

The assessee, a works contractor, was awarded a works contract by the Works Department of the Government of Bihar prior to coming into force of the GST regime.

It filed a writ petition complaining that it was being burdened to pay the GST in respect of the works allotted to it on the basis of the Schedule of Rates which did not take care of the implication of the GST.

It prayed to issue a writ of mandamus to the State to revise the Schedule of Rates so as to make it GST compliant.

The State, on the other hand, submitted that a Committee of the Rural Works Department, Government of Bihar had examined the implication of the GST Act in the light of the guidelines issued by the National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India vide Circular No. GO21(117)-320/FA, dated 6-6-2018. In accordance with the said Circular, the Bihar Rural Road Development Agency, Rural Works Department, Government of Bihar had vide letter No. 1059, dated 5-12-2018 issued under the signature of the Nodal Officer circulated the aforesaid guidelines to all the Executive Engineers which specifically provided for additional payment provision/clause.

The State also stated that the aforesaid Circular dated 6-6-2018 had also been duly considered by the Committee headed by the Engineer-in-Chief in Rural Works Department on 12-12-2018 and upon consideration the Schedule of Rates had been revised. It further submitted that on going through clause (vii) of the minutes of the meeting held on 12-12-2018 it would be evident that the grievance of the assessee had been taken care of and now the only thing that was required to be done by the assessee was to claim the differential amount on account of GST after filing of the GST return.

The applicant is engaged in business of supply of material and services of erection, testing and commissioning of supplied material in relation to electricity infrastructure.

The Ajmer Vidyut Nigam Limited (AVVNL) which provides for Rural Electricity Infrastructure for Household electrification on turnkey basis, for erection of lines, erection of single phase 11KV Sub-station and release of BPL domestic connections, awarded the above work to applicant.

The applicant filed an application for Advance Ruling seeking clarification on the questions as to whether the contract entered into with AVVNL, for supply, erection, testing and commissioning of materials/equipments for providing rural electricity infrastructure qualifies as a work contract under section 2(119) and whether it would be taxable at the rate of 12 per cent in terms of Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) as amended with effect from 25-1-2018.

The Rajasthan Authority for Advance Ruling held that the work undertaken by the applicant of supply materials/equipments and Erection, testing and commissioning of materials/equipments in building of rural electricity infrastructure is a composite supply of works contract but it is not covered under Entry No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended) and, consequentially, not eligible to be taxed at lower rate of 12 per cent (SGST 6 per cent + CGST 6 per cent) but is liable to be taxed at rate of 18 per cent (CGST 9 per cent + SGST 9 per cent).

The applicant is in agreement with observation made by AAR that the supply rendered by it is in nature of composite supply. However, it is aggrieved with Ruling that said supply is not covered under Entry No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and approached AAAR

The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFFCCIL) has awarded a contract to one 'A' (main contractor) for performance of the works relating to the design, construction, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of electrification, signaling, telecommunication and associated works of double track railway lines under construction for Bhaupur-Khurja section.

'A' (main contractor) has subcontracted the performance of certain works and services of the main contract to the applicant consisting supply and installation, testing and commissioning of automatic signaling equipment of indoor and outdoor, LC gates required as per the requirement of DFFCCIL under the main contract.

The applicant sought advance ruling in respect of the following questions:

(a)

What is the rate of tax for the subcontractor who executes the works contract work like supply of goods or services or both pertaining to Railways based on the order received from the main contractor who got the work order directly from Railways.

(b)

Does the rate of tax of 6 per cent as per Sl. No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax, dated 28-6-2017, as amended, applicable to subcontractors or not.

(c)

If the answer to the question No. (b) is yes, then from which date it is applicable.

Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, Department of Space, Government of India entered into a contract with Tata Projects Ltd., Mumbai [applicant] for design, realization, integration and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel at Thiruvananthapuram. The work involves aerodynamic structural and control design analysis, detailed design, detailed engineering, fabrication, procurement, inspection, third party inspection, loading and unloading of material, transportation to site, civil and electrical works, integration of systems, training, documentation, acceptance, testing and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel.

The applicant sought advance ruling on the following questions:

1.

Whether the supply under the contract for Design, Realization, Integration and Commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel at Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, ISRO, Thiruvananthapuram can be considered as supply of equipment eligible for the concessional rate of GST under Sl. No. 243A of Schedule I of Notification No. 1/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2018.

2.

If the above supply is considered as works contract whether it would be covered under Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 24/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017) attracting GST at the rate of 12 per cent.

The appellant is engaged in providing electrification work to APEPDCL, a State Government entity for procurement of plan, design, supply, install and commission certain facilities viz., providing underground cable work with underground power cable network on turnkey basis.

The appellant had filed an application for Advance Ruling raising following questions.

(1) Whether the tax rate of 12 per cent (CGST-6 per cent + SGST-6 per cent) is applicable to contract, in pursuance of Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 and No. 24/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017.

(2) Whether the work contract services provided to APEPDCL falls under the category of services provided to Government or a Government authority by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of with respect to certain specified works services as notified in the Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017.

The Authority for Advance Ruling had ruled that even though APEPDCL is covered under Government entity, the appellant is not entitled for the benefit of concessional rate of GST at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent under Central tax and 6 per cent State tax) in terms of Notification No. 24/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-10-2017 read with Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017, as the works undertaken by APEPDCL are for business purpose. Moreover, the transaction of the appellant comes under the works contract and falls under Entry No. (ii) of S. No. 3 of the table of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended from time to time and corresponding notifications under APGST Act, 2017, and the applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent under Central Tax and 9 per cent State Tax).

On appeal:

Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) has awarded the work of execution of civil works of Hydro Electric Project to the applicant. The work involves construction of intake structure, leading channel, tunnel, power house, tail race, civil works of switch yard, access roads and other allied works.

The applicant has sought advance ruling on issue as to whether the execution of the civil works of Hydro Electric Project would fall under Sl. No. 3(iii)(b) or 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 attracting GST at the rate of 12 per cent and whether KSEB will fall under any of the categories namely; Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity.

Applicant NBCC has entered into agreement with IIT, Bhubaneswar for Project Management Consultancy (PMC) works. The scope of the work as per the agreement includes providing and laying Sewerage and STP for residential cum academic campus, 800 seater boys hostel, 200 seater girls hostel, Construction of lecture hall complex, Construction of Student Activity Centre, Dispensary, Construction of 1000 capacity Auditorium, Construction of Directors Bunglow, 40 nos. staff Quarters, 84 nos. Faculty Quarters, Construction of Central Research & Instrumentation facilities, Construction of Central Workshop, Landscaping and allied works for academic area, construction of water works, Roof top solar PV power plants, Play grounds, Electricity, Substation DG set and fire safety measures etc.

Applicant NBCCL sought advance ruling in question as to whether the nature of supply made by applicant to IIT, BBSR vide the agreement dated 2-5-2016 is a work contract services under Central Goods and Services Tax Act (Odisha State Goods and Services Tax Act) relying on clause 119 to section 2 read with item no. 6(a) to the schedule-II. For that matter, the applicable rate of tax would be governed by Sr. No. 3 (classification code 9954) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and whether on the basis of law as well as fact, IIT, Bhubaneswar is a 'Governmental Authority' or a 'Government Entity' as defined in clause nos. (ix) and (x) in the explanation at serial no. 4 to Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (rate) dated 28-6-2017 Central GST Act and what would be applicable rate of GST.

It is also sought that whether the construction services related to sewerage project falls under clause (iii) of serial no. 3 (Classification Code 9954) of the table in the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

The appellant entered into a contract with Delhi Metro Railway Corporation (DMRC) for supply, installation, testing and commissioning of UPS systems.

Appellant is required to supply the UPS systems to DMRC and to undertake the erection, installation and commissioning of the UPS system at the sites designated by DMRC and separate consideration for supply of goods and services have been provided. The appellant has been raising separate invoices on DMRC for supply of goods and supply of services in the pre-GST as well as post-GST regime, the applicant has been treating the supplies made to DMRC as separate supply of goods and services.

In the pre-GST regime, the applicants were discharging Central Excise Duty and VAT/Sales tax on the clearance and sale of UPS system. Further, the service of erection, installation and commissioning of UPS system was treated by the appellant as 'works contract' service and thus the applicants were paying service tax accordingly.

It seeks to know whether the contract entered into with DMRC for supply, erection, installation, commissioning and testing of UPS system qualifies as supply of works contract under section 2(119).

AAR held that the supply of UPS system made by appellant to DMRC does not qualify as works contract service and, therefore, the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent in terms of Sr. No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended w.e.f. 25-1-2018) would not be available to the appellant and, it has been held that even though the supply of goods is made from Maharashtra of the appellant and supply of installation services is made from their Delhi Branch and, accordingly, both the respective registered units have raised separate invoices on DMRC, it would be treated as one single contract between DMRC and appellant. The goods and services are supplied by appellant in conjunction with each other, wherein the supply of goods (UPS) is the principal supply. Therefore, as per the AAR, the supply made by the appellant under the said contract qualifies as a composite supply in terms of sub-section (30) of section 2 and, hence, appellant would be liable to pay GST at the rate of 18 per cent on entire contract, i.e., the rate applicable to supply of UPS.

The appellant as Joint venture associate, has entered into contract with Power grid corporation of India Ltd. ('PGCIL'), one of the major Public Sector Undertakings in the State of Haryana on a Joint Venture (JV) basis along with Siemens AG, Germany as the Lead Partner and Sumitomo Electric Industries Ltd. Japan as another Partner. The contract entered by appellant with PGCIL is for on-shore and offshore supply of goods and services for complete execution of +320KV, 2 X 1000MW VSC based HVDC Terminals and DC XLPE Cable system between Pugalur and North Trichur. The said contract of supply of goods and services is divided into 6 contracts by Joint Venture.

The six contracts cover specific and detailed nature of supply of various goods and services to be executed by members of JV. Out of these 6 contracts two contracts i.e. third and fifth contracts are required to be executed by the appellant as a JV's associate. The Third Contract ('on-shore Supply Contract/Third Contract') provides for supply of equipment and materials including mandatory spares except +320KV HVDC Cable (including some of its associated items) from within India and Type Testing (as applicable), required for the complete execution of +320KV, 2 X 1000MW VSC based HVDC Terminals and DC XLPE Cable system between Pugalur and North Trichur. The Fifth Contract termed as 'onshore Service Contract (VSC part) (NOA-V)' ('on shore Service Contract/Fifth Contract') provides for the subject package, for performance of all other activities inter alia including port handling of the plant and Equipment including mandatory Spares (except +320KV HVDC Cable and some of its associated items) to be supplied from abroad, loading, inland transportation and insurance for delivery at site, insurance, unloading, storage and handling at site, installation including civil works, testing and commissioning including Performance Testing in respect of all Plant and Equipment supplied under both 'First Contract' and 'Third Contract' and any other services specified in the Bidding Documents referred to hereinabove. The scope of work under this contract as referred in the Fifth Contract is as follows:

a.

Local transportation, insurance and other incidental services

b.

Installation charges

c.

Training charges

The appellant is entrusted with the responsibility of delivery of the goods at PGCIL's site. For this, the appellant engages local transporters who issue consignment notes to the appellant for such transportation of goods and issue their freight invoices on the appellant. The appellant discharges the GST liability under reverse charge mechanism on such freight amount being paid by it to these transporters as provided under Notification No. 13/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. The appellant charges local transportation from the PGCIL as per the terms of the Service Contract. However, since the consignment note is already issued by the transporters engaged by the appellant, no subsequent additional consignment note is issued by the appellant. With respect to the local transportation charges recovered by the appellant under the aforesaid contract from the PGCIL without issuance of a consignment note, the appellant sought Advance Ruling on the applicability of tax exemption as provided under Serial No. 18 of the Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

The Advance Ruling Authority observed that the First Contract including onshore Ex-works supply of all equipment and materials cannot be executed independent of the Second Contract which is for the onshore supply of services. The two contracts are linked by a cross fall breach clause deeming that any breach in either of the contracts is to be considered to be a breach of the other contract as well. Thus, it provides the recipient with an absolute right to either terminate both the contract or claim damages accordingly. That the 'cross fall breach clause', settles unambiguously that supply of goods, their transportation to the contractee's site delivery and related services are not separate contracts, but only form parts of an indivisible composite works contract supply, as defined under section 2(119), with single source responsibility. Thus, contracts are in nature of 'Composite Supply of Works Contract', therefore should be taxable at the rate of 18 per cent.

The assessee was engaged in executing civil works contacts and was registered both under the Karnataka Value Added Tax Act, 2003 (KVAT Act) and the Central Sales Tax Act. It purchased building materials like hardware, sand and bricks falling under the Third Schedule to the KVAT Act, declared goods under section 15 of the CST Act and other non-scheduled goods from within and outside the State and from unregistered dealers. It moved an application before the Authority for Advance Clarification and Ruling for guidance on the rate of tax applicable for the execution of civil works contracts under the KVAT Act.

The AAR held that since there was no specific entry providing for the rate of tax on works contracts up to 31-3-2006, tax on goods used in the execution of works contract should be levied in accordance with the rate of tax applicable to the sale of goods under the KVAT Act 2003.

Subsequently, an order was passed in revision by the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes (Karnataka), Bangalore, holding that the orders of AAR were erroneous and prejudicial to the interests of the revenue. It was reasoned that there is a deemed sale in the course of the execution of a works contract by incorporation of the goods into the work and both before and after the amendment of section 4(1)(c) with effect from 1-4-2006, tax is levied on the taxable turnover of goods involved in the execution of a works contract.

A sales tax appeal was preferred against this order before the High Court of Karnataka which by the impugned order, allowed the appeal and set aside the order of the Commissioner. It was held that for the period prior to 1-4-2006, tax had to be levied as per section 3(1) and for the period subsequent to 1-4-2006, tax had to be levied as per section 4(1)(c).
