FACT: The applicant-company is primarily engaged in the construction business and provides works services to various customers including Government, public sector undertakings, Government entities and private sector entities.

The applicant entered into a contractual arrangement with GVSCCL, which is a limited company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 at the city level, in which the State and the urban local body (GVMC) are the promoters with 50:50 equity shareholding. The Government of India (GOI) initiated 'Smart City Mission', as a part of which Special Purpose Vehicles (SPV) are created. The SPVs will plan, appraise, approve, release funds, implement, manage, operate, monitor, and evaluate the Smart City development projects. Each Smart City will have a SPV which will be headed by a full time CEO and have nominees of Central Government, State Government and Urban Local Bodies (ULB) on its Board. GVSCCL is one of such Special Purpose Vehicles (SPV).

The applicant entered into an agreement with GVSCCL for beautification of streets including Streets cape Design, Landscaping and intersection Redesign in Visakhapatnam's Area Based development under smart Cities Mission. The agreement includes the supply of materials and provisions of services by the supplier to the applicant.

The applicant is seeking advance ruling on questions as to whether the services provided by the applicant is a composite supply of works contracts as per clauses (30) and (119) of section 2 and whether the services provided by the applicant are taxable at rate of 12 per cent as per the Sl. No. 3 (vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

HELD: The applicant is providing the supplies to the GVSCCL of (a) construction of the project; (b) development of the project including plantation, landscaping, Street lighting etc., and (c) maintenance of the project.

The Composite supply of works contract as defined at section 2 is treated as supply of service in terms of Sl. No. 6, Schedule II of CGST Act, 2017 and APGST Act, 2017.

GVSCCL is a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) created by the Government of Andhra Pradesh. GVSCCL is a limited company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 in which the Andhra Pradesh State Government and the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation are the promoters having 50:50 equity shareholding, which substantiates more than 90 per cent of participation of the Government. With reference to the 'control' wielded by the shareholders, all the directors of the board are public authorities. Initially the board was constituted with the Principal Secretary for Municipal Administration and Urban Development, Govt. of A.P. (under promoter category) as chairman. The District Collector and Commissioner, GVMC (under Promoter Category) and other 11 members were nominated by the Authorities in the State Government, ULB and Central Government as per the said G.O. The SPV is owned by the Government of A.P. and GVMC on 50:50 ratio and is governed by a Board of Directors answerable to the Government of A.P., Government of India and GVMC. The Government of A.P. and GVMC are the shareholders in the GVSCCL.

Accordingly, the GVSCCL rightly fits into the definition of the 'Government Entity' as per Sl. No. 4(x) of Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017. The functions carried out by the said GVSCCL are the functions which were entrusted by the Central Government, State Government and Local Authority i.e. of Municipal Administration.

Furthermore, the service provided by the applicant is composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2, provided to a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession. The same is classifiable under the Heading No. 9954 Entry at Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended from time to time and liable to tax at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST).

Thus, the services provided by the applicant to a composite supply of works contract as per clauses (30) and (119) of section 2 and are taxable at rate of 12 per cent under Entry No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 7]

FACT: The applicant has entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences [NCBS] for the purpose of execution of works contract for construction of building for laboratories and associated facilities at NCBS Campus in Bangalore.

It sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

What is the applicable rate of tax for the provision of construction service rendered to NCBS.

HELD: The applicant is providing works contract service to NCBS and there is no dispute whatsoever that it is a works contract service as per clause (119) of section 2. [Para 5.2]

The NCBS has obtained registration under the GST Act as a trust and the council managing this organisation has three members appointed by the Government of India, one member appointed by the Government of Maharashtra, two members appointed by the trustees of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust, the Director of the Institute (NCBS) is an ex-officio member and one co-opted member appointed by the council. Hence four members are from the Government. [Para 5.3]

The issue is whether the NCBS is covered under any one of the categories viz. Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity. It is clear at the outset itself that NCBS is not Central Government or State Government or Union Territory or a local authority. [Para 5.4]

The argument of the applicant that the NCBS is covered under the category Government Authority cannot be accepted in the light of the definition of Governmental Authority in clause (ix) of paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017). [Para 5.5]

The only question that needs to be examined is whether NCBS is a Government Entity or not. Clause (x) of paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017) defines Government Entity as:

'Government Entity' means an authority or a board or any other body including a society, trust, corporation,

(i)

Set up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature; or

(ii)

Established by any Government,

with 90 per cent or more participation by way of equity or control, to carry out a function entrusted by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or a local authority. [Para 5.6]

provided in respect of DMRC undoubtedly falls within the scope of Construction of Civil Structure provided to a person primarily in Commerce and is also used for commerce.

In section 66D(o) of the Finance Act, 1994 effective from 1-7-2012 where in respect of service of transportation of passengers by railways, distinction has been made among Metro, Monorail or Tramway which also would indicate that Monorail and Tramways are different from railways as commonly understood. HELD: The definition of 'Commercial and Industrial Construction Service' as provided in section 65(25b) excludes such activities relating to roads, ports, railways, dams, bridges, tunnels etc. There is no distinction between a monorail or metro rail or any other kind of rail and, therefore, the term 'railways' used therein has to be given its widest meaning to include all types of railways and all types of railway lines. Therefore, the distinction sought to be made by the adjudicating authority is not sustainable in law. [Para 5.1]

Notings in the Government files are not relevant for interpretation of the statutes and the statute has to be interpreted by the wordings explicitly used therein and if there is no ambiguity in the language used therein, there is no need to refer to the notings in the Government file. On that ground also, the observation of the adjudicating authority has no bearing to the facts on hand and has to be rejected. [Para 5.2]

The adjudicating authority has relied on the definition of section 66D(o) in the context of transportation of passengers by various modes such as monorail, tramways, metro rails etc. This definition came into force only with effect from 1-7-2012 but the demands in the impugned order pertain to the period prior to 1-7-2012 and, therefore, this definition has no bearing whatsoever and not applicable for interpreting the law as it stood at the relevant time. [Para 5.3]

Delhi Metro Rail is Government Railway as defined in the Indian Railway Act. If that be so, the question of levy of Service Tax under 'Commercial or Industrial Construction Service' would not arise at all as such constructions in respect of Railways stands excluded from the scope of the levy. [Para 5.4]

Indian Railway itself is an organization, which is meant to run on commercial basis. Recognizing these facts, there is a provision for a separate Railway-Budget to be presented before the Parliament and whenever there is a surplus, the Railways declared a dividend and pass it on to the Consolidated Fund of India. Therefore, the argument that only DMRC is run on commercial basis and not Indian Railway, is not an acceptable proposition. In view of the specific exclusion of 'railways' from commercial and industrial construction service, the question of imposing any Service Tax on the railways run by the DMRC does not arise at all. [Para 7]

Notification No. 12/2012-S.T., (and 25/2012-ST, Entry 14(a)) provides for exemption from Service Tax in respect of the services provided by way of construction, erection, commissioning and installation of original works pertaining to Railways, including monorail or metro. This exemption was provided when all services were brought under tax net except those specified in the negative list with effect from 1-7-2012. This exemption also clearly indicates the legislative intent of not taxing construction work pertaining to Railways. [Para 8]

Hence, demand of Service Tax on construction undertaken for Delhi Metro Rail is clearly unsustainable in law. [Para 9]

The work involves construction of intake structure, leading channel, tunnel, powerhouse, tail race, civil works of switch yard, access roads and other allied works.

The appellant had filed an application for advance ruling with regard to whether the execution of the civil works of Pazhassi Sagar Small Hydroelectric would fall under Sl. No. 3(iii)(b) or 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 attracting GST at the rate of 12 per cent and whether the rate of SGST is also 6 per cent in terms of Notification SRO 370/2017, dated 30-6-2017 for supplies covered under Work Order 06/CE CCN/2017-18, dated 6-10-2017.

The Advance ruling authority held that where appellant had been awarded work of execution of civil works of Hydroelectric Project in existing dam, it cannot be considered as civil work for canal, dam or other irrigation works eligible for concessional rate of tax but it is works contract services and rate of 6 per cent under Sl. No. 3(iii) or Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is not applicable for said services.

On appeal:

HELD: It is observed from the contents of the Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 that the following common mandatory conditions are required to be satisfied for availing concessional rate of 6 per cent Central Tax in terms of Sl.No.3 (iii) and 3(vi) of Notification 11/2017-CT (Rate):

(a) Supply must be a works contract as defined in clause 119 of section 2.

(b) Supplies must be provided to the Central Government or State Government or Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental authority or a Government entity.

(c) In the case of supplies to a Government Entity, there is a condition prescribed in proviso that the supplies should have been procured by the said Government entity in relation to a work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union territory or local authority, as the case maybe. [Para 8.1]

Further in addition to the above common conditions, Sl.No.3 (iii) of Notification 11/2017 -CT (Rate), the said supplies should be by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of canal, dam or other irrigation works, pipeline, conduit or plant for water supply. [ Para 8.2]

Further in addition to the above conditions in order to attract the rate of tax at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) as per Sl.No.3(vi) of Notification 11/2017-CT (Rate) the supply should be by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce. industry, or any other business or profession. [Para 8.3]

No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is applicable only for composite supply of works contracts as defined in clause (119) of section 2 supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of, - (a) a civil structure or any other original works, meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession. The concessional rate under this entry is not applicable for the works contract services provided as per the above work order as KSEB has been established for carrying out the business of generation, transmission and distribution of electricity in the State of Kerala on commercial principles as is evident from the provisions of sections 61 and 62 of the Electricity Act, 2003 regarding tariff regulation and determination of tariff. Therefore, the supply of works contract services as per the above work order cannot be considered as meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession. [Para 11]

The concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent under Sl. No. 3(iii) (b) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is applicable only for composite supply of works contracts as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the CGST Act, 2017. [Para 12]

It sought advance ruling on the following questions:

which is entrusted by the Government. [Para 7.5]

The Authority is not inclined to subscribe to the contentions of the applicant. The fact still remains that the sole work entrusted by the Government of Madhya Pradesh to the applicant is of generation of electricity (power) in the State of Madhya Pradesh. Construction of residential quarters though within the precincts of power plant cannot by any stretch of argument and imagination be termed as the work entrusted to applicant. [Para 7.6] The applicant has further argued that Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 provides a concessional rate of GST at 12 per cent with the conditions mentioned in Column 5 of the table as under:

'Provided that where the services are supplied to a Government Entity, they should have been procured by the said entity in relation to a work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or local authority, as the case may be.'

Now the applicant has tried to argue that it has been entrusted the work of construction of residential quarters also by the State Government. However, nothing has been placed before the Authority to substantiate such claim. In absence of any specific mention of construction of residential quarters having been entrusted to the applicant by the Government of Madhya Pradesh, there is no reason to deviate from the stand taken in the matter of application filed by Shreeji Infrastructure India (P.) Ltd.vide Order No. 15/2018, dated 18-10-2018. [Para 7.8]

However, it is a very generic question which cannot be decided without looking into specific contracts being awarded. The Authority thus refrains from giving any categorical ruling on the second question. [Para 7.9]

In view of the aforesaid, inasmuch as the tender document covered in the application is concerned, the GST will be applicable at the rate of 18 per cent under Heading No. 9954 inasmuch as it refers to construction of residential quarters, which was awarded to Shreeji Infrastructure (P.) Ltd. [Para 7.10]

Ruling

The work contract awarded to Shreeji Infrastructure (P.) Ltd. for construction of residential quarters at Thermal Power Project shall attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) under Heading No. 9954. [Para 8.1]

GST with respect to the services rendered by the sub-contractor to the main contractor i.e. the applicant would be applicable at the rate of 12 per cent in view of Entry (vi) and (iv) of the CGST Rate Notification read with the UPGST Rate Notification or at the rate of 18 per cent?

HELD: As the question number I & II asked by the applicant are interrelated, both the questions are taken-up together for discussion. [Para 8] As regard to the classification of supply made by the applicant to the NHAI under Entry No. (iv) or (vi) to Sl. No. 3 of the Notification No. 11/2017 C.T. (R), dated 28-6-2017, it is observed that the said Entry No. (iv) reads as follows :

'(iv) Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2, supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of, —

(a)

a road, bridge, tunnel, or terminal for road transportation for use by general public;

Whereas the Entry No. (vi) of the said Notification reads as :

'Composite supply of works contract as defined under clause (119) of section 2, provided to the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of -

(a)

a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession;

Provided that where the services are supplied to a Government Entity, they should have been procured by the said entity in relation to a work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union territory or local authority, as the case maybe.'

and in both the cases the applicable rate of GST is at the rate of 12 per cent including CGST and SGST.

Now, it is observed that the question to be decided is :

(i)

Whether the supply made by the applicant to the NHAI is a 'composite supply of works contract', and, if yes,

(ii)

Whether the said supply is being used for construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of a road, bridge, tunnel, or terminal for road transportation for use by general public, or

(iii)

Whether the said supply is being provided to the Central Government, Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of -

(a)

a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession;

(iv)

Which classification will be more appropriate among Entry (iv) or Entry (vi) of the CGST Rate Notification. [Para 10]

As per the sub-section (30) of section 2 , the 'Composite supply' is defined to mean a supply made by a taxable person to a recipient consisting of two or more taxable supplies of goods or services or both, or any combination thereof, which are naturally bundled and supplied in conjunction with each other in the ordinary course of business, one of which is a principal supply.

Further the term 'works contract' is defined in sub-section (119) of section 2 to mean a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property, wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract. [Para 11]

It is observed that the agreement entered into between the applicant and NHAI is for the 'Development of six lane Eastern Peripheral Expressway : ITS (Intelligent Transport System) Installation Project', which involves design, supply, installation, testing, commissioning of ITS which primarily includes Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS), Toll Management System (TMS) and Digital Transmission System along with operation and maintenance of ATMS for a period of 4 years on turnkey basis. From this, it appears that the scope of work involves supply of goods as well as services, which are in conjunction with each other to complete the ITS installation. [Para 12]

As per the General Conditions of the contract entered between the applicant and NHAI, each item of plant and materials shall become the property of the NHAI and free from liens and other encumbrances at the earlier of the (a) when it is incorporated in the works (b) when the applicant is paid the corresponding value of the plant and materials. [Para 13]

3(vi) to the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 covers a wide spectrum of construction services as composite supply.

Sl. No. 3(vi) to the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 provides a concessional rate of GST at the rate of 12 per cent subject to condition provided under column (5), which reads as: Provided that where the services are supplied to a Government Entity, they should have been procured by the said entity in relation to a work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union territory or local authority, as the case may be. [Para 7.8]

In the instant case, the applicant has been awarded a consolidated contract for carrying out different specified works at the Thermal Power Project, which includes erection, commissioning, installation, etc. There are certain items mentioned in the subject contract including, but not limited to, 'Fitness Centre cum Gym', which definitely do not find place in the ambit of essential work entrusted by the State Government to MPPCGL. Needless to mention that such work shall not qualify for exemption as envisaged under Sl. No. 3(vi) to the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 inasmuch as it does not fall within the scope of work entrusted by the State Government to MPPGCL. [Para 7.9]

In view of the aforesaid, the work entrusted vide subject tender document/contract awarded to the applicant by MPPGCL cannot be termed as composite supply. Thus the entire work under contract shall not be entitled to concessional rate in terms of Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. However, the supply of goods and/or services which squarely fall within the ambit of scope of work entrusted to MPPGCL by the State Government of Madhya Pradesh shall be entitled for concessional rate under Sl. No. 3(vi) to Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. Accordingly each and every supply under the subject contract shall be treated separately for determining the rate of tax under the CGST Act, read with the provisions of GST Tariff and respective exemption Notifications. [Para 7.10]

Ruling

The tender document in question is not a consolidated contract and each supply under the said contract shall be chargeable to tax individually, depending upon the individual classification of such supplies and rate of tax applicable at the time of supply. [Para 8.1]

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant has constructed residential complexes for Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) - Whether since control over BDA rests with Govt. of Karnataka, BDA is a Government entity - Held, yes - Whether activity undertaken by applicant involves supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property and, hence, is a 'works contract' within meaning of section 2(119) - Held, yes - Whether transaction of applicant would be a supply of works contract services covered under clause (a) of Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, taxable at rate of 12 per cent GST - Held, yes [Paras 10.8, 10.9.2  11]GST : Where applicant has constructed residential complexes for Bangalore Development Authority (BDA), activity undertaken by applicant is supply of works contract service to a Govt. entity covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, taxable at rate of 12 per cent GST

Work Contract Services - Composite supply pertaining to railways - Construction service - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Period 2018-19 to 2022-23 - Assessee was a joint venture formed for executing various railway projects in India - Assessee was assigned works contract by RVNL for ‘Doubling of track, construction of roadbed, minor bridges, platforms, buildings, water and effluent treatment facilities, wagon/coach maintenance infrastructure, supply of ballast, installation of tracks and other electrical, signalling, and telecommunication infrastructure’ - During period April, 2018 to March, 2019, assessee paid GST at rate of 12 per cent on above contract - Assessee had discharged taxes at rate of 12 per cent on premise that said contract constitutes works contract services of original works pertaining to Railways covered under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) - Further, assessee was served with an intimation in Form GST DRC-01A - Said notice proceeds on premise that said contract between assessee and RVNL was liable to tax at 18 per cent, instead, assessee had erroneously discharged taxes at a lower/concessional rate of 12 per cent on works contract executed by assessee - Thereafter demand order was also confirmed by revenue for differential tax of 6 per cent - HELD : Expression ‘pertaining to’ employed in said notification with reference to railways is one of very wide import - Use of expression ‘pertaining to’ would show that legislation intended to give an expansive meaning to expression ‘Railway’ - Phrase ‘pertaining to’ has been interpreted in previous Supreme Court rulings as broad and inclusive, covering activities closely related to primary subject - In instant case assessee's contract clearly relates to railway development and expression ‘pertaining to’ ensures that infrastructure projects were aiding railway operations; even if carried out by a subsidiary like RVNL, same would still constitute original work pertaining to railway for purpose of subject notification and, thus, covered under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of said notification - Thus, activity of assessee would be covered under concessional rate and there was no reason to exclude assessee’s works contract from ambit of 12 per cent rate [Section 9, read with section 73, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 16.1 16.2, 17.2 and 18.4] [In favour of assessee]

Railway infrastructure construction - Construction services - Composite supply of works contract - Words contract - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Contract for supply of goods and services was awarded to assessee by RITES Ltd., a Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) on behalf of South Eastern Coalfield Limited (SECL) for construction of railway infrastructure facilities for proposed feeder line of East West Rail Corridor within leasehold boundary of project for coal evacuation through Rail - Aforesaid supply involves supply of goods and services which are supplied in conjunction with each other in ordinary course of business; same is to be considered as composite supply under section 2(30) - Such supply being original work in terms of Para 2(zs) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 pertaining to Railway network owned by a SECL, a PSU is to be considered as original work pertaining to Railways under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and is specifically covered under Heading No. 9954 21 - However, since term Works Contract defined under section 2(119) is restricted to contract for building construction, fabrication etc. of any immovable property only and Letter of acceptance issued by RITES to applicant-assessee only outlines description of their activities which appears to be Project Management Consultancy services, it is not possible to conclusively hold that their activities are covered under Works Contract under said section 2(119) - Hence, works proposed to be performed by them under LOA would attract 12 per cent GST under SL. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended vide Notification No. 1/2018-C.T. (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 subject to condition that same satisfies definition of Works Contract under section 2(119) otherwise it would be taxable at rate of 18 per cent GST under Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Chhattisgarh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 1, 2.2 to 2.4, 7 to 7.8, 7.10 and 8] [Partly in favour of assessee]GST : Supply of goods and services for construction of railway infrastructure facilities for feeder line of Rail Corridor owned by South Eastern Coalfield Limited for evacuation of coal, under contract awarded by RITES, a PSU, is specifically covered under SAC 9954 21 and same is considered to be an original work pertaining to Railways and a composite supply in terms of section 2(30); therefore, such supply would attract 12 per cent GST subject to condition that it satisfies definition of works contract under section 2(119), otherwise it would be taxable at rate of 18 per cent GST   GST : Term 'pertaining to Railways' occurring in Entry 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017as amended includes both Government Railways as well as non-Government Railways

Construction for Railways - Works contract service - Contractor and sub-contractor - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Advance ruling sought on supply of works contract service to Indian Railways in capacity of contractor as well as sub-contractor - HELD: Works contract services supplied to Indian Railways such as construction of rail under bridge and construction of tunnels are covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate) and GST is payable at 18 per cent - Such works contract services supplied to Indian Railways through main contractor in capacity of a sub-contractor is also covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(xii) of said notification and GST is payable at 18 per cent [Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 9] [In favour of assessee]GST : Supply of works contract services of construction for Indian Railways either as a main contractor or in capacity of a sub-contractor through main contractor, is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and GST is payable at 18 per cent  GST : Supply of works contract services involving predominantly earthwork to Indian Railways either as a main contractor or in capacity of a sub-contractor, is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and GST is payable at 12 per cent  GST : Supply of ballast to Indian Railways is covered under Heading 2517 and is liable to GST at 5 per cent in terms of entry at Sl. No. 126 of Schedule I to Notification No. 01/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended vide Notification No. 1/2018-C.T. Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of residential colony - Heading 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant is engaged in construction of residential and commercial complexes - It has been awarded a contract by Airport Authority of India for construction of residential colony staff and employees - Whether construction of residential colony by applicant attracts GST at rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) as per entry at SI. Construction of railway siding - Construction service - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Public sector undertaking, Rites Limited has, for and on behalf of Eastern Coalfields Limited, awarded applicant different works in connection with construction of new railway siding - Works undertaken by applicant is in relation to immovable property and involve transfer of property in goods thereby qualify to be 'works contract' - Construction work in connection of new railway sidings undertaken by applicant is to be considered as original works as defined in clause 2(zs) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Ministry of Railways, Government of India in its Freight Marketing Circular No. 11 of 2016 issued on 22-8-2016 has also recognized 'private siding' for railway freight services - Therefore, construction of private sidings pertains to railways and is taxable at rate of 12 per cent under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 till omission of said entry vide Notification No. 3/2022- Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017][Paras 4.5, 4.6, 4.9 and 4.10] [In favour of assessee]GST : Construction of new railway siding is 'works contract' and also qualifies to be 'original works' pertaining to railways; same is taxable at rate of 12 per cent under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 till its omission

Railway infrastructure construction - General Construction services of highways, streets, roads, railways, etc - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Advance ruling is sought on whether civil works undertaken for Indian government enterprise for railways in connection with construction of rail infrastructure for providing railway siding for dispatch of washed and raw coal is eligible for concessional rate of GST at 12 per cent - HELD: GST is applicable at 12 per cent only when service provided relates to construction and in nature of composite supply of works contract and should qualify as original works pertaining to railways - Work undertaken is covered under "General construction services of highways, streets, roads, railways, airfield runways, bridges and tunnels" classifiable under Heading 9954 - Work undertaken amounts to composite supply or cannot be conclusively answered in absence of sufficient evidence - Although it is apparent from work undertaken that it is supply in relation to immovable property, there must also be transfer of property in goods in execution of contract - Work undertaken for RITES qualifies as original works pertaining to railways which will be liable to GST at 12 per cent if same qualifies as composite supply of works contract [Chhattisgarh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 8] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where works were undertaken for Indian government enterprise for railways namely, RITES qualifies as original work pertaining to railways, GST at 12 per cent will be available if said work qualifies as composite supply of works contract

Classification of services - Kerala State Goods And Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services)- Section 2(119), of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant is engaged in providing services of construction including materials and labour as per tender requirements - They have received a work order from Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre for construction of a building for space transportation system - It is a composite contract which includes supply of materials as well as service - They have also received another work order from Infrastructure Kerala Ltd., a Public Private Partnership Company promoted by Government of Kerala, for development of Medical College which includes construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure - Applicant has requested for advance ruling on rate of tax applicable for above works contracts awarded by Government authorities - Whether since services provided by applicant under both contracts fall under definition of works contract under section 2(119) and services are being provided to Central Government and State Government, applicant is eligible for concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended - Held, yes [Para 9]GST: Where services of construction with material provided by applicant under construction contracts awarded by Government authorities fall under definition of works contract under section 2(119) and services being provided to Central and State government, applicant will be eligible for concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3 (vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017, dated 28-6-2017

Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Installation, commissioning and fitting out of a civil structure - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, Department of Space, Government of India entered into a contract with Tata Projects Ltd., Mumbai [applicant] for design, realization, integration and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel at Thiruvananthapuram - Work involves aerodynamic structural and control design analysis, detailed design, detailed engineering, fabrication, procurement, inspection, third party inspection, loading and unloading of material, transportation to site, civil and electrical works, integration of systems, training, documentation, acceptance, testing and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel - Whether supply under contract can be considered as supply of equipment eligible for concessional rate of GST as per Sl. No. 243B of Schedule I of Notification No. 1/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, no - Whether work of design, realization, integration and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel as a turnkey project will fall under definition of works contract - Held, yes - Whether service provided by applicant to Central Government by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession will attract 12 per cent GST as per Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 6] [Partly in favour of assessee]GST : Where Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre entered into a contract with Tata Projects Ltd., Mumbai [applicant] for design, realization, integration and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel, supply under contract cannot be considered as supply of equipment and work as a turnkey project will fall under definition of works contract and service provided by applicant will attract 12 per cent GST

Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Services provided by sub-contractor to main contractor pertaining to railways - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways - It executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract - Whether tax rate to be charged by applicant to main contractor would be at rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST - Held, yes [Para 11] [In favour of assessee]GST: Where applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways and it executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract, tax rate to be charged by applicant to main contractor would be at rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Civil Construction and works contract services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services)/Section 2(119) of the Central Goods And Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant is engaged in business of Civil Construction and Works Contract Services - It has entered into agreement to undertake subcontract work of civil construction of residential complexes/row of residential houses which in turn has been allotted to GIPL (main contractor) through tender by Bengaluru Development Authority - Whether since projects of applicant are involving supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property it is a 'work contract' within meaning of section 2(119) - Held, yes - Whether works contract is for construction of a civil structure and since it is a residential real estate project, works is predominantly for use other than commerce, industry or any other business or profession and it is covered under clause (a) of entry 3(vi) of Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes - Whether further, since main contractor is providing services specified in item 3(vi) of Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, subcontract work of works contract provided by applicant as a subcontractor to main contractor is covered under item (ix) of entry 3 of Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification No. 1/2018 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, taxable at 6 per cent CGST with effect from 25-1-2018 - Whether however, for period from 1-7-2017 to 24-1-2018, same is taxable at 9 per cent CGST - Held, yes [Paras 11 and 12]GST: Projects of applicant involving work orders from Principal contractor for civil construction of residential complexes consisting of supply of both goods and services in relation to an immovable property is a 'works contract' within meaning of section 2(119)   GST: Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Entity within meaning of Notification No.11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Composite supply of works contract services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant has been awarded contracts by 3 Electric Distribution companies- HESCOM, MESCOM and BESCOM, comprising of work in nature of strengthening of distribution networks on Turnkey Basis, providing infrastructure to regularized IP sets by extending electric lines, erection of distribution transformers, and strengthening works - Contracts executed by applicant are works contract, because (i) they are in relation to completion, erection, installation, and commissioning of an immovable property as all projects are turnkey projects and property in goods cannot be removed without dismantling same, and (ii) there is transfer of property involved in execution of contract - Further, distribution companies are involved in supply of goods and hence are involved in business of supplying goods and also receive consideration for supply of electricity - Predominant activity of electricity distribution companies is to supply electricity and works executed by applicant are used for this predominant activity only and hence are original works meant predominantly for use for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession - Whether therefore, it was to be held that services provided by applicant to Energy Supply Companies (wholly owned Government of Karnataka Undertakings) by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion etc. are not covered under entry 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 12/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, or under entry 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended from time to time and consequently are not eligible to be taxed at a lower rate of 12 per cent GST and hence are liable to be taxed at 18 per cent GST - Held, yes [Paras 11 and 12]GST: Services by way of construction erection, commissioning, installation, completion etc. provided by applicant to Energy Supply Companies(wholly owned Government of Karnataka Undertaking) are liable to be taxed at 18 per cent GST

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 [Construction Services] - Applicant a Private Limited Company entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences(NCBS) for construction of Hostel building at NCBS Campus in Bangalore - It sought advance ruling on whether it should charge GST at rate of 12 per cent for service provided to NCBS as per Notification No 24/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 21-9-2017- It is found that NCBS, which is a separate centre of Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), receives grant from Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India and that NCBS is neither set-up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature nor was established by any Government, but is an autonomous body under aegis of TIFR - Moreover, council administering this institute has only 4 members appointed by Government and therefore Government does not have more than 90 per cent control over it - Thus, NCBS is not covered under definition of a 'Government Entity' as per clause (x) of para 4 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Furthermore, Institute is not established to carry out a function entrusted by Government, thus, it is not covered by clause (vi) of serial no. 3 of Notification - Whether therefore, service supplied by applicant to NCBS is not taxable at concessional rate of 12 per cent and is taxable at 18 per cent under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 5 and 6]GST: Works contract service provided by applicant to National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) for construction of hostel building on campus is taxable at 18 per cent GST under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant is engaged in business of execution of works contracts relating to electrical works and electrical infrastructure - Applicant has been allocated electrical sub-contractor works by first sub-contractor 'S' which in turn is sub-contracted by main contractor 'O' who have been awarded contract by 'K' for civil, electrical and mechanical works - 'K' is a company which is wholly owned by Government of Karnataka - Whether since there is no privity of contract between applicant and main contractor i.e., 'O' and contract is between applicant and 'S' 'which is not covered under Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority or a Governmental Authority or Government Entity, supply made by applicant is not covered under Entry No. 3 (iii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes - Whether activity of applicant is also not covered under Entry Nos. 3(vi) and 3(ix) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes - Whether thus, composite supply undertaken by applicant is not covered under Entry No. 3(iii) or 3(vi) or 3(ix) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and, hence, applicant is not eligible to charge GST at a concessional rate of 12 per cent - Held, yes - Whether applicant has to discharge tax at rate of 18 per cent under provision of GST Act - Held, yes [Paras 9.4, 10.2, 10.3 and 12]GST : Where applicant has been allocated electrical sub-contractor works by first sub-contractor 'S' which in turn is sub-contracted by main contractor 'O' who have been awarded contract by 'K' for civil, electrical and mechanical works, composite supply undertaken by applicant is not covered under Entry No. 3(iii) or 3(vi) or 3(ix) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and, hence, applicant is not eligible to charge GST at concessional rate of 12 per cent and is liable to GST at rate of 18 per cent

Construction of Roads and Bridges - Construction Services - Heading 9954 - Classification - Applicant is a contractor engaged in construction of roads and bridges - Applicant seeks advance ruling on what is GST rate on works contract services provided by a Government Contractor to KSTP, construction of Roads and bridges for public use?- Held : In instant case, recipient of applicant i.e., Kerala State Transport Project (KSTP) is a wing constituted under Kerala Public Works Department was to execute externally aided projects and specialized projects - Main aim of this wing is upgradation of State highway roads - Strategic option study made for upgradation of State highways and major district roads led to formation of KSTP under Kerala Public Works Department - Government had accepted study report and accorded administrative sanction for upgradation of 1719.46 kilometers of roads vide GO (MS). 142/97/PWD dated 22-12-1997 of Public Works (D) Department, Government of Kerala through KSTP with aid of World Bank - Hence, works contract services provided by applicant to KSTP by way of construction of roads and bridges is for use of general public - As such, rate of tax for works contract services provided by applicant to KSTP by way of construction of roads and bridges for public use will be taxable at 12 per cent (CGST at rate 6 per cent and SGST at rate 6 per cent) - Further, as per Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 amended by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022, it is evident that till 17-7-2022, rate of tax for works contract services by way of construction of roads and bridges for public use was 12 per cent (CGST at rate 6 per cent and SGST at rate 6 per cent), if, time of supply as determined in accordance with section 14 falls any date prior to 18-7-2022, otherwise it will be taxable at 18 per cent (CGST at rate 9 per cent and SGST at rate 9 per cent) [Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.6-7.10] [Against assessee]
