FACT: The applicant was engaged in providing works contract service as sub-contract to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways. The assessee filed instant application to sought clarification for rate of tax to be levied by it to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways. The assessee submitted that it should be charged 12 per cent GST only and not 18 per cent as applicable in other cases.

HELD: The applicant has submitted that they are supplying Works Contract Services (WCS), as a sub-contractor, to the main contractor who in turn are supplying WCS for original work pertaining to the Railways. They have made further submissions that when a contractor awards either wholly or partially, the work to a sub-contractor, then the work to be performed by both of them remains the same and identical to what is specified in the contract between the main contractor and the employer, in this case, the railways and as per Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 22-8-2017 the rate of GST is 12 per cent for composite supply of works contract supplied by way of construction, erection, commission or installation of original works pertaining to railways. They are claiming that since the tax rate is 12 per cent for the main contractor, the same rate should be applicable to them too. They have also submitted that Notification No.-01/2018-Central Tax (Rate) dated 25-1-2018 has made certain amendments to the earlier Notification No. 20/2017, but has not provided clarification with respect to services provided by sub-contractor to main contractor for railway original works contract services. They have also cited SR. No. -12 in press release of 25th meeting of GST council held at New Delhi on 18-1-2018, and stated that the rate of GST applicable to main contractor should be levied by sub-contractor.

Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, has specified the rate of central tax to be levied on Intra State supply of services of description specified in column 3 of the table in the said Notification, falling under scheme of classification of services mentioned therein. The relevant clauses (v) as mentioned by the applicant in their favour, of the said Notification, as amended by Notfn No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 22-10-2017.

The applicant has submitted that they are supplying Works Contract Services (WCS), as a sub-contractor, to the main contractor who in turn are supplying WCS for original work pertaining to the Railways. They have made further submissions that when a contractor awards either wholly or partially, the work to a sub-contractor, then the work to be performed by both of them remains the same and identical to what is specified in the contract between the main contractor and the employer, in this case, the railways and as per Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 22-8-2017 the rate of GST is 12 per cent for composite supply of works contract supplied by way of construction, erection, commission or installation of original works pertaining to railways. They are claiming that since the tax rate is 12 per cent for the main contractor, the same rate should be applicable to them too. They have also submitted that Notification No.-01/2018-Central Tax (Rate) dated 25-1-2018 has made certain amendments to the earlier Notification No. 20/2017, but has not provided clarification with respect to services provided by sub-contractor to main contractor for railway original works contract services. They have also cited SR. No. -12 in press release of 25th meeting of GST council held at New Delhi on 18-1-2018, and stated that the rate of GST applicable to main contractor should be levied by sub-contractor.

Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, has specified the rate of central tax to be levied on Intra State supply of services of description specified in column 3 of the table in the said Notification, falling under scheme of classification of services mentioned therein. The relevant clauses (v) as mentioned by the applicant in their favour, of the said Notification, as amended by Notfn No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 22-10-2017.

A plain reading of Sr. No. 3, clause (v) reveals that 'composite supply of WCS supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation of original works pertaining to, railways attracts a tax rate of 6 per cent each of CGST and SGST. The applicant has submitted that they have been sub-contracted by the main contractor to supply WCS and in turn the main contractor is supplying WCS to the railways. From the submissions made by the applicant it appears that the WCS provided by them is the same or a part of the main contract entered into between the main contractor and the railways. It also appears that works contract service is civil works performed by the sub-contractor for the railways and the property in goods (materials used in the supply of Works Contract Service) also gets transferred to the railways directly. In such a case as per the abovementioned clause (v) of Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 22-10-2017, the works contract service provided by the sub-contractor to the main contractor would be supply of works contract pertaining to railways and, therefore, chargeable to tax at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent of CGST and SGST each). However, the benefit of 12 per cent tax rate would be available to the applicant only if the Works Contract services provided by them are Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation of original works pertaining to railways. Thus, in respect of Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 dated 28-6-2017 as amended up till today, even the sub-contractor providing services of composite supply of works contract in respect of original works pertaining to railways would be covered for concessional rate of GST at the rate of 12 per cent as given under Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 as amended referred above. [Para 5]

The tax rate to be charged by the sub-contractor to the main contractor would be at the rate of 6 per cent of CGST and SGST each, in the present case. The tax rate to be charged would be 12 per cent in the present case. [Para 6]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Supply and installation - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFFCCIL) has awarded a contract to one 'A' (main contractor) for performance of works relating to design, construction, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of electrification, signaling, telecommunication and associated works of double track railways lines under construction for Bhaupur-Khurja section - 'A' (main contractor) has subcontracted performance of certain works and services of main contract to applicant - Whether contract work of applicant to main contractor is covered under Entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to tax at 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST or 12 per cent IGST) with effect from 22-8-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 4.10 and 5][In favour of assessee]GST: Where Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited has awarded a contract to one 'A' (main contractor) for performance of works relating to railways and 'A' has sub-contracted performance of certain works and services of main contract to applicant, contract work of applicant to main contractor is covered under Entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

FACT: The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFFCCIL) has awarded a contract to one 'A' (main contractor) for performance of the works relating to the design, construction, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of electrification, signaling, telecommunication and associated works of double track railway lines under construction for Bhaupur-Khurja section.

'A' (main contractor) has subcontracted the performance of certain works and services of the main contract to the applicant consisting supply and installation, testing and commissioning of automatic signaling equipment of indoor and outdoor, LC gates required as per the requirement of DFFCCIL under the main contract.

The applicant sought advance ruling in respect of the following questions:

(a)

What is the rate of tax for the subcontractor who executes the works contract work like supply of goods or services or both pertaining to Railways based on the order received from the main contractor who got the work order directly from Railways.

(b)

Does the rate of tax of 6 per cent as per Sl. No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax, dated 28-6-2017, as amended, applicable to subcontractors or not.

(c)

If the answer to the question No. (b) is yes, then from which date it is applicable.

HELD: The contract of the applicant with the main contractor should satisfy the following conditions to get covered under Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017:

(a)

The contract must be a composite supply of works contract.

(b)

The works must be a construction, erection, commissiong or installation of original works.

(c)

It must pertain to Railways. [Para 4.4]

In the instant case, the contract is for supply and installation, testing and commissioning of automatic signaling equipment of indoor and outdoor, LC gates and involves excavation of pits, casting and plastering and other parts which involve construction, erection, commissioning and installation of original works. Hence the second condition is satisfied.

As the contract is related to an immovable property, the entire contract is covered under the definition of works contract under section 2(119). Hence the first condition is also satisfied. [Para 4.5]

The main issue is whether this is a contract pertaining to Railways. The main contractor has obtained the contract from Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited and then subcontracted to the applicant. The work is related to supply and installation, testing and commissioning of automatic signaling equipment of indoor and outdoor, LC gates as per the requirement of DFCCIL. [Para 4.6]

Since the works related to railways network, the contract can be said to be pertaining to Railways. The term pertaining to Railways is more expansive and includes other establishments other than Indian Railways. Hence the contract is pertaining to Railways. [Para 4.8]

FACT: The applicant has been awarded a contract by one Rites Limited, which is a Public Sector Undertaking. Said contract is awarded for execution of works of laying of track as per layout plan, pavement along the track, construction of Admin building, Warehouse, Electrical works and Fire-fighting works, etc. at Khodiyar Gandhinagar, Gujarat. Further contract is involving both supply of goods and services and is a composite supply in the nature of works contract supply.

The applicant sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

Whether the said work can be covered under clause 3(v)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, i.e., works contract by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to railways so as the entitle it for charging rate of GST at the rate of 12 per cent instead of 18 per cent.

HELD: Entry No. 3(v)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017, reads as :

Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 by ways of construction, erection, commissioning or installation by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to, -

(a)

Railways, including monorail and metro-----; [Para 13]

The contract of the applicant should satisfy the following conditions to get covered under the aforesaid Entry No. 3(v)(a):

(i)

The contract must be a composite supply of works contract;

(ii)

The works must be a construction, erection, commissioning or installation by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works;

(iii)

It must pertain to railway. [Para 14]

The work awarded to the applicant comprises of laying of track as per layout plan, pavement along the track, construction of Admin building, Warehouse, Electrical works and Fire-fighting works, etc. at Khodiyar, Gandhinagar, Gujarat. FACT: The applicant is engaged in the business of Civil Construction and Works Contract Services. The applicant has applied for the civil construction work tender with Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) with respect to construction of residential complexes/row of residential houses.

The said project is allotted to the applicant and the same has been executed by the Company through appointing various contractors.

The applicant has sought advance ruling in respect of the question as to whether the activity undertaken by the applicant is covered under section 2(119); whether Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Authority as per the provisions of GST Law and the rate of tax applicable to the transaction of the applicant and more so whether the transactions are covered under entry 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 (as amended).

According to applicant, its activity of construction of residential house and residential complex with respect to following BDA projects (to Government Authority) are squarely covered under the definition of Works Contract and their activity will be considered as supply of services.

The applicant submits that as per the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), the activity undertaken by the applicant to BDA i.e., Government Authority is liable for GST at 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST.

HELD: For a works contract to be covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 the following conditions needs to be satisfied:

(a)

The recipient of services must be a Government Entity and in this case, Bangalore Development Authority;

(b)

The works contract services supplied by the applicant must be in relation to the works covered under (a), (b) or (c) of Entry 3(vi);

(c)

The recipient of such services must have procured these services in relation to a work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or local authority. [Para 10.6]

Bangalore Development Authority is an authority established by the State Government under the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 and it is entrusted with the activity of development of the City of Bangalore and areas adjacent thereto and for matters connected therewith. [Para 10.7]

The control over the entity rests with the Government of Karnataka and, hence, the Bangalore Development Authority satisfies both the conditions and, hence, is considered as a Government Entity within the meaning of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017. [Para 10.8]

The applicant is constructing a Housing Project at two places in and around Bangalore. The Bangalore Development Authority in its tender has stated that it has taken up construction of housing in and around Bangalore City as designed by the Government of Karnataka. Since this is a residential project for general public, the same is not covered under clause (b) or (c) of Entry 3(vi). [Para 10.9.1]

Coming to the next question for which Advance Ruling is required, the Authority noticed that the Notification No. 1/2018- Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 has been issued by the Central Government making amendments in the Notification No. 8/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. Previously, under the Notification dated 28-6-2017, composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 was attracting duty at the rate of 18 per cent under Heading 9954 (Construction Services) at Sl. No. 3.

Vide Notification No. 20/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017, the entries against serial number 3 for item (iii) in column (3) and the entries relating thereto in the Notification No. 1/2018- Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, were substituted with (v) Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 , supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to,- (a) railways, excluding monorail and metro; attracting the duty rate at the rate of 12 per cent.

Later, vide Notification No. 1/2018- Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, the Notification No. 8/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate), was amended and the word `excluding' was substituted by 'including' also classifying that the Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor providing services specified in item (iii) or item (vi) above to the Central Government, State Government, Union territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity would attract duty at the rate of 12 per cent.

Since, in the instant case, the composite supply of work contract is being provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor i.e. Government Authority, the same shall be covered under the above amendment carried out vide the above notification dated 25-1-2018, the same shall now attract duty at the rate 12 per cent.[Para 9.4]

In view of the above, both the members unanimously rule as under;

(i)

A contract shall be treated as Composite Contract under GST if it involves making of supply of goods and services which are inter-connected and inter­-dependent on each other even though BOQ mentions separate value of goods and services.

(ii)

A pre-GST period contract shall be treated as Composite Contract in GST if it satisfies the condition of Composite Supply.

(iii)

A contract for designing, installation and setting up of Automatic Fare Collection System for Lucknow Metro Project will amount to Work Contract.

(iv)

GST will be charged at the rate of 12 per cent in terms of Notification No. 1/2018- Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 being composite services supplied to a Government entity procured by the said entity in relation to work entrusted to it by the Central and State Government.[Para 10]

The applicant is constructing a Housing Project at two places in and around Bangalore. The Bangalore Development Authority in its tender has stated that it has taken up construction of housing in and around Bangalore City as designed by the Government of Karnataka. Since this is a residential project for general public, the same is not covered under clause (b) or (c) of Entry 3(vi). [Para 10.9.1] The projects of the applicant are involving the supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property and, hence, is a 'works contract' within the meaning of section 2(119) of CGST Act. This works contract is for a construction of a civil structure and since it is a residential real estate project, the works is predominantly for use other than commerce, industry or any other business or profession and, hence, it is covered under clause (a) of the Entry No. 3(vi) of the Notification, subject to the conditions. [Para 10.9.2]

Regarding the issue as to whether the recipient has procured the said services in relation to a work entrusted to it by the State Government, it is observed that the Bangalore Development Authority Act, which is passed by the State Legislature, has entrusted the activity of development of the City of Bangalore and areas adjacent thereto and for matters connected therewith to the BDA and the Authority has to obtain the sanction of the Government of Karnataka for every scheme they propose to implement. Hence, the condition is also satisfied. [Para 10.9.3]

Hence the services provided by the applicant to the Bangalore Development Authority in relation to the construction of two housing complexes referred to in the application are covered under entry no. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 (as amended) and is liable to tax at 6 per cent under the CGST Act, 2017. Similarly, the services provided is covered under entry no. 3(vi)(a) of Notification (11/2017) No. FD 48 CSL 2017 dated 29-6-2017 (as amended) and is liable to tax at 6 per cent under the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. [Para 10.9.4]

Thus, activity undertaken by the applicant as enumerated in the application is covered under section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act and is a works contract services. Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Entity as per the provisions of the GST Law. The transaction of the applicant would be a supply of works contract services covered under clause (a) of Entry No. 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 (as amended) and not under Entry No. 3(ii) or 3(iv) or 3(v) of the said notification. The main issue is whether the work awarded to the applicant is contract pertaining to railways. In the instant case, the work relating to construction has been awarded by an entity viz. Rites Ltd. 'Railways' has not been defined under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. Section 2(31) of the Railways Act, 1989 defines railways as :

(31) 'railway' means a railway, or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods, and includes -

(a)

all lands within the fences or other boundary marks indicating the limits of the land appurtenant to a railway;

(b)

all lines of rails, sidings or yards, or branches used for the purposes of, or in connection with, a railway;

(c)

all electric traction equipment's, power supply and distribution installations used for the purposes of, or in connection with, a railway;

(d)

all rolling stock, stations, offices, warehouses, wharves, workshops, manufactures, fixed plant and machinery, roads and streets, running rooms, rest houses, institutes, hospitals, water works and water supply installations staff dwellings and any other works constructed for the purpose of, or in connection with, railway;

(e)

all vehicles which are used on any road for the purposes of traffic of a railway and owned, hired or worked by a railway; and

(f)

all ferries, ships, boats and rafts which are used on any canal, river, lake or other navigable inland waters for the purposes of the traffic of a railway and owned, hired or worked by a railway administration, but does not include -

(i)

a tramway wholly within a municipal area; and

(ii)

lines of rails built in any exhibition ground, fair, park or any other place solely for the purpose of recreation; [Para 14.3.1]

Further , sections 2(20) and 2(25) of the Railways Act, 1989 define 'Government railway' and 'non-Governmental railway' as :

(20) 'Government railway' means a railway owned by the Central Government;

Previously, under the Notification dated 28-6-2017, composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 was attracting duty at the rate of 18 per cent under Heading 9954 (Construction Services) at Sl. No. 3.

Vide Notification No. 20/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017, the entries against serial number 3 for item (iii) in column (3) and the entries relating thereto in the Notification No. 1/2018- Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, were substituted with (v) Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 , supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to,- (a) railways, excluding monorail and metro; attracting the duty rate at the rate of 12 per cent.

Later, vide Notification No. 1/2018- Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, the Notification No. 8/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate), was amended and the word `excluding' was substituted by 'including' also classifying that the Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor providing services specified in item (iii) or item (vi) above to the Central Government, State Government, Union territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity would attract duty at the rate of 12 per cent.

Since, in the instant case, the composite supply of work contract is being provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor i.e. Government Authority, the same shall be covered under the above amendment carried out vide the above notification dated 25-1-2018, the same shall now attract duty at the rate 12 per cent.[Para 9.4]

In view of the above, both the members unanimously rule as under;

(i)

A contract shall be treated as Composite Contract under GST if it involves making of supply of goods and services which are inter-connected and inter­-dependent on each other even though BOQ mentions separate value of goods and services.

(ii)

A pre-GST period contract shall be treated as Composite Contract in GST if it satisfies the condition of Composite Supply.

(iii)

A contract for designing, installation and setting up of Automatic Fare Collection System for Lucknow Metro Project will amount to Work Contract.

(iv)

GST will be charged at the rate of 12 per cent in terms of Notification No. 1/2018- Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 being composite services supplied to a Government entity procured by the said entity in relation to work entrusted to it by the Central and State Government.[Para 10]

Thus, there is a natural bundle of goods and services per cost center/Line and the supply is construed to be made when the entire supply of the line/cost center is made. Hence, the supply of the applicant is a composite supply and this criterion is satisfied. [Para 11.2]

The next criterion to be examined is whether the said composite supply is a 'Works Contract' as defined under section 2(119). From the definition, a work shall be treated as Works Contract if that work is done for land or earth or for immovable property and there is transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of such contract. Immovable property cannot be moved. It cannot be separated from the land or earth. If it is detached it shall have to destroy. In the case at hand, the 'Employer's Requirements, Particular Specifications-4B Telecommunication General Specification' - gives the outline summary of the various systems and sub-systems which are applicable to the Telecommunication scope and the outline description of the works said to be the works of the applicant. On going through same, it is observed that the work involves installation of the individual systems at platforms, stations, other select locations along the corridor and is integrated at the Operation Control Corridor (OCC) at Koyambedu and the Telecommunications Infrastructure implementation is to be synchronized with the civil construction phases. Further the scope of works of the applicant like Public Address and Voice Alarm System, CCTV System, Passenger Information Display System, Office Telephone System, etc. requires installation on specific locations, namely ceiling and the like and these goods once installed, may not necessarily be damaged while removing. The applicant has not established with documents that the works contracted to them are to be executed on immovable property as required under definition of 'Works Contract' given above. The applicant has stated that in the Pre-GST regime, under Service Tax, the applicant being a supplier of Works Contract Service relating to infrastructure project of railways, in capacity of sub-contractor was exempted from service tax and had claimed the benefit of entry 3(v) of Notification 11/2017 - C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as above. The definition of 'Works Contract' as it existed in the 'Service Tax' law is different from that defined under section 2(119) of GST Act. Under GST, only those defined works carried out on any immovable property is covered under 'Works Contract'. Thus without documentary proof of the works contracted/undertaken like related diagrams/plans/schedules/Pictures/detailed write-up on the works, etc. in the absence of submission of the entire sub-contract agreement, it is not possible for this Authority to conclude that the works are done on the immovable property and once installed, the goods/equipments cannot be dismantled without damage so as to hold that the work undertaken is 'Works Contract' as per section 2(119) of the Act. As the applicant has stated that it will not be possible for them to furnish the entire sub-contract agreement which contains the requisite details, in the absence of the documentation works could not be said as 'Works Contract' as per section 2(119). [Para 11.3]

The other criteria to be satisfied are the supply should be by way of 'construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works' pertaining to railways, including monorail and metro. Original work is defined in Para 2(zs) of the Notification No. 12/2017 - C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

From the submissions, it is seen that the work of the applicant includes Installation of the various systems on designing, manufacture and supply and therefore is 'Original work' as defined in the notification.

The work of the applicant is on the lines, stations and locations of land appurtenant and, therefore, this criterion is satisfied. [Para 11.4]

To summarize, the entry at 3(v) do not specify the class of service provider to whom it applies. The entry is specific to the composite supply of works contract pertaining to railways including monorail and metro. This view is fortified by the justification of the recommendation of the Fitment Committee to the 25th GST Council meeting (available in Volume-2 of the Agenda) after which the downward revision of the rate was effected.

22.2-4 Plant & machinery assembled at site is works contract and hence 'supply of service'

Plant and Machinery or structure assembled and erected at site is 'works contract'.

The word 'goods' applies to those which can be brought to market for being bought and sold, and it is implied that it applies to such goods as are movable. Goods erected and installed in the premises and embedded to earth cease to be goods and cannot be held to be excisable goods. - Quality Steel Tubes (P.) Ltd. v. CCE 75 ELT 17 = (1995) 2 SCC 372 = 1995 AIR SCW 11 - in this case, it was held that tube mill and welding head erected and installed in the premises and embedded in the earth for manufacture of steel tubes and pipes are not 'goods'.

In Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Indian Oil Corporation AIR 1991 SC 686 = 1991 Supp (2) SCC 18, it was held that if the chattel is movable to another place in the same position (condition?), it is movable property. If it has to be dismantled and re-erected at later place, it is attached to earth and is immovable property - followed in Triveni Engineering v. CCE 2000 AIR SCW 3144 = 40 RLT 1 = 120 ELT 273 (SC), where it was observed, 'The marketability test requires that the goods as such should be in a position to be taken to market and sold. If they have to be separated, the test is not satisfied'.

In Precision Automation and Robotics India Ltd. In re (2018) 69 GST 713 = 97 taxmann.com 319 (AAR-Maharashtra), it has been held that supply and installation of 'car parking system' qualifies as immovable property and hence is works contract, as the car parking system, once erected, cannot be removed without dismantling.

22.3 Tax Rate of works contract as composite supply

Legislature can prescribe uniform rate of tax for all goods involved in works contract, even though different rates are prescribed for sale of such goods - State of Karnataka v. Durga Projects Inc. (2018) 4 SCC 633 (SC 3 member bench).

Sr No. 3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) and No. 8/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017, effective from 1-7-2017 prescribes rate of 18% (9% CGST and 9% SGST) or 18% IGST on composite supply of works contract as defined in section 2(119) of CGST Act.

However, in my view, works contract is a composite supply and rate cannot be 18% in all cases. Since it is a composite supply, GST rate should depend on the principal supply.

FACT: The applicant is carrying on business in the housing and construction sector. They are engaged in providing services of construction including materials and labour as per the tender requirements. They have received a work order from Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre for the construction of a building for space transportation system. They have also received another work order from a Public Private Partnership Company promoted by Government of Kerala, for the development of Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram which includes construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure.

The applicant has requested for advance ruling on the rate of tax applicable for the above works contracts awarded by the Government authorities.

HELD: As per section 2(119), 'works contract' means a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract.[Para 5]

On a perusal of the work orders and the agreements entered by the applicant it is clear that the services rendered by the applicant clearly falls within the definition of works contract under section 2(119).[Para 6]

Since the services provided by the applicant under both the contracts fall under the definition of works contract under section 2(119) and the services being provided to the Central Government and State Government, the applicant is eligible for the concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended.

In view of the observations stated above, it is ruled that the services provided by the applicant under both the contracts being composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 provided to the Central Government and State Government by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry or any other business or profession is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended and attract GST at the rate of 12 per cent [6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST].

[Para 11.10.2] Regarding the issue as to whether the recipient has procured the said services in relation to a work entrusted to it by the State Government, it is observed that the Bangalore Development Authority Act, which is passed by the State Legislature, has entrusted the activity of development of the City of Bangalore and areas adjacent thereto and for matters connected therewith to the BDA and the Authority has to obtain the sanction of the Government of Karnataka for every scheme they propose to implement. Hence for the reasons stated above, the services provided by GIEPL to Bangalore Development Authority in relation to the construction of housing complexes are covered under clause (a) of entry no.3(vi) of the Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended from time to time. The applicant has entered into subcontract agreement with the main contractor and this is in relation to the activity covered under entry No 3(vi) of the Notification No.11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. Classification of services - West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Erection, commissioning and installation of original work pertaining to railways - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Applicant is engaged in activity of providing technological and system solutions - Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) awarded it contract for extension of its Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) - Applicant makes supply to 'RVNL' by way of erection, commissioning, installation, completion etc. of said SCADA system - Whether, in view of facts, applicant is making a composite supply of works contract taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as being erection, commissioning and installation of original work pertaining to railways, including metro - Held, yes [Para 4.10]GST: Where Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) awarded a contract to applicant for 'extension of its Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) and applicant makes supply to RVNL by way of erection, commissioning, installation, completion etc. of SCADA system, applicant is making a composite supply of works contract taxable under Entry No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as being erection, commissioning and installation of original work pertaining to railways, including metro

, Staff recreation like parks, new rain water harvesting structures, painting, renovation of old structures etc. The applicant has claimed before the Railway Authorities that these are all original works as they involve new asset creation or bringing life to unused structures of Railways and these come under the works contract services as per CGST Act. [Para 9]

The issue is basically divided into two categories. One that results in the new buildings and the other repair and reconstruction of the old structures. [Para 10] The rate of tax applicable in terms of Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is 6 per cent under CGST. [Para 10.1]

Entry 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is related to works contract services supplied to Railways, which is construction or erection or commissioning or installation of original works. The entire dispute is regarding what are 'original works'. [para 10.2]

The term 'original works' has been defined in clause (zs) of para 2 of Notification No. 12/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 10.3]

On examination of definition of 'original work', it is seen that only 'additions or alterations made to abandoned or damaged structures on land that are made to make them workable' are treated as original works and not all repairs and maintenance services. [Para 10.4]

The works carried out by the applicant are analyzed and it is found that they involve two types of works - one being new construction and other being repairs of old structures. In as far as construction of new structures are concerned which are constructed where nothing existed before would definitely fall under the realm of 'original works'. [Para 10.5]

But in case of constructions which are made where the structures already existed, the same can be classified as (a) where the additions and alternations are made to the abandoned structures on land or damages structures on land to make them workable; (b) repairs of already existing structures which are in working condition and (c) construction services on structures not on land.

It is pertinent to note that only those works contract services covered under (a) are to be treated as 'original works' and not those covered under related to (b) and (c). The meaning of the words 'structures on land' needs to be analysed as only these qualify for the reduced rate of tax. [Para 10.6]

Both the contextual meaning in relation to railways is that the structure should be something which is built from parts, i.e., a building, or other constructed ones. Secondly, these constructed structures should be on land to be covered under the scope of the entry. All these point to the scope of the entry that the structures which are directly on the land are included. Further, these structures must be damaged to the extent that the same cannot be used and the activity of works contract services, if executed to make these unusable structures reusable, would cover under this entry for reduced rate of tax. [Para 11]

All repairs made to buildings do not constitute 'original works'. It is only those services executed to make an unusable building usable again is covered under 'original works'. [Para 13]

The Railways Department is a Central government Department and, hence, it is clear that the services provided to them if it is for a purpose other than for business, then the same would be covered under entry 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. However, the services of repairs, maintenance, renovation and alterations of residential complex meant for use of the Railway employees are covered under entry 3(vi) of the Notification and, hence, eligible for tax at 6 per cent CGST. [Para 14]

As regards the question of rate of tax, it is submitted by the applicant that the contract is a single contract and it consists of multiple works. On the question whether this contract amounts to a composite supply or mixed supply or a bunch of separate supplies, it is seen that the same cannot be a composite supply of works contracts as there is no principal supply and the works are not naturally bundled. It cannot be a mixed supply also because the valuations of each of the supply of works are valued separately and they would amount to separate contracts. Hence, there is no common price for all the contracts. Hence, it can be decided that each of the works mentioned in a schedule is a separate contract in itself and this is bolstered by the fact that the works are not in the same place and also are different in nature. [Para 15]

CONSTRUCTION FOR RAILWAY COACH FACTORY - NOT TAXABLE : 3. Our company has executed works contract for Rail Coach Factory (RCF) Kapurthala. The nature of work is "Extension of gantry (a type of structure) in front of Sheet Metal Shop in workshop area". The work involved supply and erection of PEB structures of steel. The period of works contract was from 1st April, 2009 to 31st March, 2012. The value of the contract was say Rs. 1 crore. The service tax department is asking for payment of service tax on works executed for RCF. The company is of the view that RCF is railways and the works executed for Railway is exempted from service tax. But the service tax department is of the view that RCF is commercial activity, since the coaches manufactured by it are put to commercial use by the Railways. We understand that the definition of Railways as per Railways Act includes workshop. Thus, work executed by the company would not be liable to service tax. Use of manufactured coaches is a separate thing. Construction or erection of the workshop for coaches is a separate thing.

You may kindly enlighten us whether the stand of the company is correct that construction & erection of gantry in workshop area of railway is not taxable.

Railway is defined in section 2(31) of the Railways Act, 1989. Sub-clause (d) of the said definition reads as under : -

"railway" means a railway, or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods, and includes-

….

(d)

all rolling stock, stations, officers warehouses, wharves, workshops, factories, fixed plant and machinery, roads and streets, running rooms, rest houses, institutes, hospitals, water works and water supply installations, staff dwellings and any other works constructed for the purpose of, or in connection with, railway;

…

The relevant taxable services, viz., Commercial construction services and works contract services exclude services/works contracts in respect of roads, airports, railways, transport terminals, bridges, tunnels and dams.

It appears that the construction work done by you would fall under sub-clause (d) of the definition above and would be 'in respect of' railways and not liable to service tax.

For a works contract to be covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 the following conditions needs to be satisfied:

(a)

The recipient of services must be a Government Entity and in this case, Bangalore Development Authority;

(b)

The works contract services supplied by the applicant must be in relation to the works covered under (a), (b) or (c) of Entry 3(vi);

(c)

The recipient of such services must have procured these services in relation to a work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or local authority. [Para 10.6]

Bangalore Development Authority is an authority established by the State Government under the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 and it is entrusted with the activity of development of the City of Bangalore and areas adjacent thereto and for matters connected therewith. [Para 10.7]

The control over the entity rests with the Government of Karnataka and, hence, the Bangalore Development Authority satisfies both the conditions and, hence, is considered as a Government Entity within the meaning of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017. [Para 10.8]

The applicant is constructing a Housing Project at two places in and around Bangalore. The Bangalore Development Authority in its tender has stated that it has taken up construction of housing in and around Bangalore City as designed by the Government of Karnataka. Since this is a residential project for general public, the same is not covered under clause (b) or (c) of Entry 3(vi). [Para 10.9.1]

The projects of the applicant are involving the supply of both goods and services and is in relation to an immovable property and, hence, is a 'works contract' within the meaning of section 2(119) of CGST Act. This works contract is for a construction of a civil structure and since it is a residential real estate project, the works is predominantly for use other than commerce, industry or any other business or profession and, hence, it is covered under clause (a) of the Entry No. 3(vi) of the Notification, subject to the conditions. [Para 10.9.2]

Regarding the issue as to whether the recipient has procured the said services in relation to a work entrusted to it by the State Government, it is observed that the Bangalore Development Authority Act, which is passed by the State Legislature, has entrusted the activity of development of the City of Bangalore and areas adjacent thereto and for matters connected therewith to the BDA and the Authority has to obtain the sanction of the Government of Karnataka for every scheme they propose to implement. Hence, the condition is also satisfied. [Para 10.9.3]

Hence the services provided by the applicant to the Bangalore Development Authority in relation to the construction of two housing complexes referred to in the application are covered under entry no. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 (as amended) and is liable to tax at 6 per cent under the CGST Act, 2017. Similarly, the services provided is covered under entry no. 3(vi)(a) of Notification (11/2017) No. FD 48 CSL 2017 dated 29-6-2017 (as amended) and is liable to tax at 6 per cent under the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. [Para 10.9.4]

Thus, activity undertaken by the applicant as enumerated in the application is covered under section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act and is a works contract services. Bangalore Development Authority is a Government Entity as per the provisions of the GST Law. The transaction of the applicant would be a supply of works contract services covered under clause (a) of Entry No. 3(vi) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 (as amended) and not under Entry No. 3(ii) or 3(iv) or 3(v) of the said notification. [Para 11]

The works are supply and installation of lines and equipments meant for telecommunication, signalling in the CMRL project and not related to any civil engineering work. Therefore, the supply of the applicant to Siemens is covered under SAC 9954, more specifically under SAC 995461 and the first requirement of the entry stands satisfied. [Para 11.1]

The second criteria to be satisfied is that the supply should be a 'Composite Supply'. In the case at hand from the purchase order furnished by the applicant, it is seen that there is supply of goods (equipments, goods, etc.) and services (installation, testing, etc.) for a particular cost center/Line and the work is considered to be done on that basis. Thus, there is a natural bundle of goods and services per cost center/Line and the supply is construed to be made when the entire supply of the line/cost center is made. Hence, the supply of the applicant is a composite supply and this criterion is satisfied. [Para 11.2]

The next criterion to be examined is whether the said composite supply is a 'Works Contract' as defined under section 2(119).

From the definition, a work shall be treated as Works Contract if that work is done for land or earth or for immovable property and there is transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of such contract. Immovable property cannot be moved. It cannot be separated from the land or earth. If it is detached it shall have to destroy. In the case at hand, the 'Employer's Requirements, Particular Specifications-4B Telecommunication General Specification' - gives the outline summary of the various systems and sub-systems which are applicable to the Telecommunication scope and the outline description of the works said to be the works of the applicant. On going through same, it is observed that the work involves installation of the individual systems at platforms, stations, other select locations along the corridor and is integrated at the Operation Control Corridor (OCC) at Koyambedu and the Telecommunications Infrastructure implementation is to be synchronized with the civil construction phases. Further the scope of works of the applicant like Public Address and Voice Alarm System, CCTV System, Passenger Information Display System, Office Telephone System, etc. requires installation on specific locations, namely ceiling and the like and these goods once installed, may not necessarily be damaged while removing. The applicant has not established with documents that the works contracted to them are to be executed on immovable property as required under definition of 'Works Contract' given above. The applicant has stated that in the Pre-GST regime, under Service Tax, the applicant being a supplier of Works Contract Service relating to infrastructure project of railways, in capacity of sub-contractor was exempted from service tax and had claimed the benefit of entry 3(v) of Notification 11/2017 - C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as above. The definition of 'Works Contract' as it existed in the 'Service Tax' law is different from that defined under section 2(119) of GST Act. Under GST, only those defined works carried out on any immovable property is covered under 'Works Contract'. Thus without documentary proof of the works contracted/undertaken like related diagrams/plans/schedules/Pictures/detailed write-up on the works, etc. in the absence of submission of the entire sub-contract agreement, it is not possible for this Authority to conclude that the works are done on the immovable property and once installed, the goods/equipments cannot be dismantled without damage so as to hold that the work undertaken is 'Works Contract' as per section 2(119) of the Act. As the applicant has stated that it will not be possible for them to furnish the entire sub-contract agreement which contains the requisite details, in the absence of the documentation works could not be said as 'Works Contract' as per section 2(119). [Para 11.3]

The other criteria to be satisfied are the supply should be by way of 'construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works' pertaining to railways, including monorail and metro. Original work is defined in Para 2(zs) of the Notification No. 12/2017 - C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

From the submissions, it is seen that the work of the applicant includes Installation of the various systems on designing, manufacture and supply and therefore is 'Original work' as defined in the notification.

The work of the applicant is on the lines, stations and locations of land appurtenant and, therefore, this criterion is satisfied. [Para 11.4]

To summarize, the entry at 3(v) do not specify the class of service provider to whom it applies. The entry is specific to the composite supply of works contract pertaining to railways including monorail and metro. This view is fortified by the justification of the recommendation of the Fitment Committee to the 25th GST Council meeting (available in Volume-2 of the Agenda) after which the downward revision of the rate was effected.

The applicant submitted before the Authority that the work involves supply, erection, testing and commissioning including transport, loading, unloading, insurance, etc. of transformer substation, HT & LT Overhead Line & Cable through underground for the Metro Rail Project. In the tender/work order, the work schedule separately describes each activity to be carried out to complete the work and also rate for each activity is separately mentioned. By adding amount of each activity total estimated tender cost is derived and it has quoted in per cent above or below of the estimated cost. Thus it had no option to quote the individual prices for each activity and the tender had to be accepted as a whole and it could not accept part activities. It has further stated that NMRCL is insisting it to charge 12 per cent GST as per Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018- Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 treating above work as composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the CGST Act, 2017, supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation of original works pertaining to, - (a) railways, including monorail and metro. It has also submitted that it is of the view that it is not supplying works contract service because in the instant case there is no involvement of immovable property. It said that the supply should be classified as composite supply, as different goods and services viz. testing, cable, wires, cement pipes, laying, joints, insurance, commissioning, transport, etc. are naturally bundled and supplied in conjunction with each other, with principal supply being LT/HT cable.

HELD: The basic issue before the Authority is as to whether in the instant case there is supply of works contract or not.

In view of this, the applicant contends that scope of the activity of works contract cannot be restricted to an activity undertaken only in relation to immovable property and the scope can be extended to the services rendered in relation to plant and machinery also. Firstly the term 'works contract' is clearly defined in section 2(119). The definition is self explanatory and leaves no doubt that it is in relation to an immovable property only. Secondly, in section 17(5), the term 'plant and machinery' is also defined. Here the machinery, apparatus and equipment is secured to the earth by way of a foundation or structural support. This foundation or the structural support is meant to impart stability to the machine while working. It, however, does not impart the machine/equipment the same degree of permanence that a building acquires when built on its foundation. Here the equipment is fitted on the foundation and the same can be removed and relocated without damaging it. The same does not hold true for a building or an immovable property. Therefore, the inference drawn from the provisions of section 17(5) are erroneous.

The applicant is executing two types of works wherein, in one set of work the applicant is executing works contract for construction of new buildings and in the second set of work, it is executing works contracts not involving new construction. The correspondence of the applicant with the Railways revealed that in Zonal Works, majority of the works, it is executing are like provision of compound wall to Railway properties, laying of tiles for buildings, plumbing with new pipelines, provisions of new GLR and OHT, Staff recreation like parks, new rain water harvesting structures, painting, renovation of old structures etc. The applicant has claimed before the Railway Authorities that these are all original works as they involve new asset creation or bringing life to unused structures of Railways and these come under the works contract services as per CGST Act. [Para 9]

The issue is basically divided into two categories. One that results in the new buildings and the other repair and reconstruction of the old structures. [Para 10]

The rate of tax applicable in terms of Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is 6 per cent under CGST. [Para 10.1]

Entry 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is related to works contract services supplied to Railways, which is construction or erection or commissioning or installation of original works. The entire dispute is regarding what are 'original works'. [para 10.2]

The term 'original works' has been defined in clause (zs) of para 2 of Notification No. 12/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 10.3]

On examination of definition of 'original work', it is seen that only 'additions or alterations made to abandoned or damaged structures on land that are made to make them workable' are treated as original works and not all repairs and maintenance services. [Para 10.4]

The works carried out by the applicant are analyzed and it is found that they involve two types of works - one being new construction and other being repairs of old structures. In as far as construction of new structures are concerned which are constructed where nothing existed before would definitely fall under the realm of 'original works'. [Para 10.5]

But in case of constructions which are made where the structures already existed, the same can be classified as (a) where the additions and alternations are made to the abandoned structures on land or damages structures on land to make them workable; (b) repairs of already existing structures which are in working condition and (c) construction services on structures not on land.

It is pertinent to note that only those works contract services covered under (a) are to be treated as 'original works' and not those covered under related to (b) and (c). The meaning of the words 'structures on land' needs to be analysed as only these qualify for the reduced rate of tax. [Para 10.6]

Both the contextual meaning in relation to railways is that the structure should be something which is built from parts, i.e., a building, or other constructed ones. Secondly, these constructed structures should be on land to be covered under the scope of the entry. All these point to the scope of the entry that the structures which are directly on the land are included. Further, these structures must be damaged to the extent that the same cannot be used and the activity of works contract services, if executed to make these unusable structures reusable, would cover under this entry for reduced rate of tax. [Para 11]

All repairs made to buildings do not constitute 'original works'. It is only those services executed to make an unusable building usable again is covered under 'original works'. [Para 13]

The Railways Department is a Central government Department and, hence, it is clear that the services provided to them if it is for a purpose other than for business, then the same would be covered under entry 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. However, the services of repairs, maintenance, renovation and alterations of residential complex meant for use of the Railway employees are covered under entry 3(vi) of the Notification and, hence, eligible for tax at 6 per cent CGST. [Para 14]

The applicant is a supplier of services as per work order issued for execution by the Railways. From examination of the LOA and the annexed Schedules, it is clear that the work to be executed involves repair, maintenance and fitting out of immovable property, namely, Railway Tracks, and also transfer of property in goods in course thereof. It is, therefore, a 'Composite Supply' of labour and goods in the nature of Works Contract, as defined under section 2(119) and is, therefore, classifiable under (ii) of Column 3 (Description of Service) of Heading 9954 (Construction services) of column 2 under serial No. 3 of column 1 of the Table in Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 under the CGST Act, 2017 (1135-FT, dated 28-6-2017 under the WBGST Act, 2017. The services rendered by the applicant are to be classified under SAC (Service Code Tariff) Heading 9954, Group 99542, Sub-group 995429. [Para 3]

The works contract service of maintaining railway track as per the above LOA is, taxable at the rate of 18 per cent under the Serial No. 3(ii) of the Rate Notification. Thus, the applicant supplies works contract service, as defined under section 2(119) of the GST Act, of maintaining existing railway tracks, which is taxable at the rate of 18 per cent under serial No. 3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 under the CGST Act, 2017 (1135-FT, dated 28-6-2017 under the WBGST Act, 2017). The appropriate SAC (Service Code Tariff) is. Heading 9954, Group 99542, Sub-group 995429. [Para 6]

In order to answer this question, the nature of a contract as well as documents submitted by the appellant in relation to execution of the project have to be gone through. It is seen from the nature of contract which envisages installation, which involves civil works to erect the structure for execution of the project in its entirety. It is an entire system comprising of a variety of different structures which are installed after a lot of prior work which involves detailed designing, ground work. Appellant has also submitted few photographs of the project which clearly shows that the structure is attached to the earth with the help of civil work. The photographs indicate the magnitude of the work done. Further foundations in cement concrete, cement concrete walls as well as cement concrete structures are constructed during the execution of the project. The mode of annexation shows that the groundwork, being the necessary foundation, is an important part of the project. The object of annexation, as said earlier, cannot be to make it movable from one place to the other. It simply cannot be equated to the Asphalt mix (the issue in Solid & Concrete Engg. case) which was intended to be moved from one place to other. Hence considering the scope of the work and the facts revealed by the photographs, it can be very well said that completion of the installation, erection of the total project is resulting into immovable property. Hence the total project assigned to the appellant is nothing but composite supply of works contract as envisaged under section 2 (119). [Para 53]

CONSTRUCTION NOT IN RESPECT OF RAILWAYS - TAXABLE

1. Our company has executed works contract for Central Rail Side Warehousing Corporation Ltd. (CRWC) at Ranchi (Jharkhand). The nature of works is construction, erection and installation of PEB structures of steel and incidental works for warehouse complex. The period of contract executed is 1st April, 2007 to 31st March, 2012. The service tax department is asking for payment of service tax for the contract value of this work of say Rs. 1 crore.

We understand that Railways is exempted from service tax. The definition of railways as given in the Railways Act includes its warehouses. So, our company should not be liable to service tax on such works contract of construction, erection and installation of warehouses. Use of the warehouses is not exempted but construction of railway warehouses is exempted.

Constitution of CRWC is as follows: Indian Railways have entered into a MOU with the Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) as its strategic partner for development of integrated railside warehouse complexes. CWC has created a SPV as its subsidiary, named as CRWC with the sole purpose of developing railside warehousing complexes (not other complexes). The Indian Railways has provided land near various railway terminals and the CRWC has constructed and erected railway warehousing complexes on the land by contracting with our company. Indian Railway will get its share of profit by way of profit sharing from CRWC.

Kindly enlighten us whether the stand of the company is correct that construction of railside warehousing by Indian Railways in partnership with CRWC should not be taxable.

Railway is defined in section 2(31) of the Railways Act, 1989; the same is reproduced below -

"railway" means a railway, or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods, and includes-

"(a)

all lands within the fences or other boundary marks indicating the limits of the land appurtenant to a railway;

(b)

all lines of rails, sidings, or yards, or branches used for the purposes of, or in connection with, a railway;

(c)

all electric traction equipments, power supply and distribution installations used for the purposes of, or in connection with, a railway;

(d)

all rolling stock, stations, officers warehouses, wharves, workshops, factories, fixed plant and machinery, roads and streets, running rooms, rest houses, institutes, hospitals, water works and water supply installations, staff dwellings and any other works constructed for the purpose of, or in connection with, railway;

(e)

all vehicles which are used on any road for the purposes of traffic of a railway and owned, hired or worked by a railway; and

(f)

all ferries, ships, boats and rafts which are used on any canal, river, lake or other navigable inland waters for the purposes of the traffic of a railway and owned, hired or worked by a railway administration,

but does not include-

(i)

a tramway wholly within a municipal area; and

(ii)

lines of rails built in any exhibition ground, fair, park or any other place solely for the purpose of recreation.

The relevant taxable services, viz., Commercial construction services and works contract services exclude services/works contracts in respect of roads, airports, railways, transport terminals, bridges, tunnels and dams.

The query can be answer solely on basis of clause (d) of the definition, as it lists various places to be considered as 'railways'.

Services provided by railway include transport of passengers and goods and, constructions necessary therefor are covered by the term 'railways'. The words "officers warehouses"... "rest houses"... "any other works" … "for the purpose of railways" or "in connection with railways" are wide enough to cover warehouses meant for storage of goods transported by the railways.

If that is the case, the services will be considered as having been provided in respect of construction of warehouse for use of the railways.

However, construction of warehouses meant for commercial use by railways and not for use of railways will not be covered under 'railways' and services provided would be not considered as 'in respect of' railways.

Please note that the services must be provided "in respect of" railways and not merely "to" railways.

Hence, it appears that the services provided by your client would be liable to service tax.

The argument of the applicant that the NCBS is covered under the category Government Authority cannot be accepted in the light of the definition of Governmental Authority in clause (ix) of paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017). [Para 5.5]

The only question that needs to be examined is whether NCBS is a Government Entity or not. Clause (x) of paragraph 4 of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 31/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017) defines Government Entity as:

'Government Entity' means an authority or a board or any other body including a society, trust, corporation,

(i)

Set up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature; or

(ii)

Established by any Government,

with 90 per cent or more participation by way of equity or control, to carry out a function entrusted by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or a local authority. [Para 5.6]

provided in respect of DMRC undoubtedly falls within the scope of Construction of Civil Structure provided to a person primarily in Commerce and is also used for commerce.

In section 66D(o) of the Finance Act, 1994 effective from 1-7-2012 where in respect of service of transportation of passengers by railways, distinction has been made among Metro, Monorail or Tramway which also would indicate that Monorail and Tramways are different from railways as commonly understood. HELD: The definition of 'Commercial and Industrial Construction Service' as provided in section 65(25b) excludes such activities relating to roads, ports, railways, dams, bridges, tunnels etc. There is no distinction between a monorail or metro rail or any other kind of rail and, therefore, the term 'railways' used therein has to be given its widest meaning to include all types of railways and all types of railway lines. Therefore, the distinction sought to be made by the adjudicating authority is not sustainable in law. [Para 5.1]

Notings in the Government files are not relevant for interpretation of the statutes and the statute has to be interpreted by the wordings explicitly used therein and if there is no ambiguity in the language used therein, there is no need to refer to the notings in the Government file. On that ground also, the observation of the adjudicating authority has no bearing to the facts on hand and has to be rejected. [Para 5.2]

The adjudicating authority has relied on the definition of section 66D(o) in the context of transportation of passengers by various modes such as monorail, tramways, metro rails etc. This definition came into force only with effect from 1-7-2012 but the demands in the impugned order pertain to the period prior to 1-7-2012 and, therefore, this definition has no bearing whatsoever and not applicable for interpreting the law as it stood at the relevant time. [Para 5.3]

Delhi Metro Rail is Government Railway as defined in the Indian Railway Act. If that be so, the question of levy of Service Tax under 'Commercial or Industrial Construction Service' would not arise at all as such constructions in respect of Railways stands excluded from the scope of the levy. [Para 5.4]

Indian Railway itself is an organization, which is meant to run on commercial basis. Recognizing these facts, there is a provision for a separate Railway-Budget to be presented before the Parliament and whenever there is a surplus, the Railways declared a dividend and pass it on to the Consolidated Fund of India. Therefore, the argument that only DMRC is run on commercial basis and not Indian Railway, is not an acceptable proposition. In view of the specific exclusion of 'railways' from commercial and industrial construction service, the question of imposing any Service Tax on the railways run by the DMRC does not arise at all. [Para 7]

Notification No. 12/2012-S.T., (and 25/2012-ST, Entry 14(a)) provides for exemption from Service Tax in respect of the services provided by way of construction, erection, commissioning and installation of original works pertaining to Railways, including monorail or metro. This exemption was provided when all services were brought under tax net except those specified in the negative list with effect from 1-7-2012. This exemption also clearly indicates the legislative intent of not taxing construction work pertaining to Railways. [Para 8]

Hence, demand of Service Tax on construction undertaken for Delhi Metro Rail is clearly unsustainable in law. [Para 9]

(a) Supply must be a works contract as defined in clause 119 of section 2.

[Para 8.3]

[Para 12]

The applicant-Joint Venture (JV) is engaged in the business of constructions of infrastructure project. The said JV was formed on 27-12-2008 to undertake work of 'construction of tunnel and its allied works in Pune under Krishna Bhima Stabilization project. The Godavari Marathwada Irrigation Development Corporation allotted above mentioned work to the applicant. The applicant submit that the work order is consisting of earth work such as excavation for tunnel, removing of excavated stuff, providing steel support, rock bolting, reinforcement, fixing of chain link, cement concreting etc. wherein earth work is more than 75 per cent of total work. The applicant further submits that since the work i.e. earth work constitute more than 75 per cent of the total work in term of value, they are covered by Entry No. 3 of Notification No. 12/2017, dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017 and effective from the said date where GST is payable at the rate of 5 per cent (CGST 2.5 per cent and SGST 2.5 per cent).

It is found that the concessional rate of tax as per Entry No. 3(vii) is available to those composite supply of works contract where the earth work constitute more than 75 per cent of the value of the works contract. The mute question, therefore, in instant application vis-a-vis Notification Entry No. 3(vii) is to decide whether the contract involves earth work. The expression earth work has not been defined in the GST Act, Rules and the notifications.

From the meaning assigned the expression earth work as per Dictionary, the term earth work means the structure made from earth especially an embankment or construction made of earth. On perusal of tender documents it is found that the present work is the construction of tunnel and its allied work and therefore said work cannot be considered as earth work contemplated by Entry No. 3(vii).

From the perusal of entire entry at Sl. No. 3 it is opined that Entry No. 3(iii) is the most appropriate entry in the instant case.

In the 'detailed tender notice' issued by Godavari Marathwada Irrigation Development Corporation, Aurangabad through Executive Engineer, it is stated that the function and power of the corporation have been listed in the Maharashtra Act XXIII of 1998. In general, it has been entrusted with the work of investigation, planning, designing of projects, maintenance of completed projects, construction of projects and irrigation management of the major, medium and minor projects in the Godavari River Basin. The projects comprise of irrigation hydroelectric project (except Bhandardara (Phase-I and II) and Ghatghar Hydro Electric Power Projects) along with the command area development and multipurpose schemes. In view of this, instant transaction can be considered as other irrigation work. [Para 6]

Thus, the said contract is not covered under Sl. No. 3A, Chapter No. 99 as per Notification No. 2/2018-Central Tax (Rate) dated 25-1-2018, with effect from 25-1-2018.

The said contract is not covered under the term 'earth work' and, therefore, not covered under Heading No. 9954 as per Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 13-10-2017. [Para 7]

As per the sub-section (30) of section 2 , the 'Composite supply' is defined to mean a supply made by a taxable person to a recipient consisting of two or more taxable supplies of goods or services or both, or any combination thereof, which are naturally bundled and supplied in conjunction with each other in the ordinary course of business, one of which is a principal supply.

Further the term 'works contract' is defined in sub-section (119) of section 2 to mean a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property, wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract.
